srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text:
Must define DiffTest as the following named struct in package testutils:

  type DiffTest struct {
      Name          string                 // subtest name used with t.Run; required
      Args          []string               // command-line arguments passed to both binaries
      Stdin         []byte                 // nil = no stdin (both binaries receive EOF immediately)
      Env           []string               // nil = use defaults only (LC_ALL=C); non-nil = KEY=VALUE pairs merged into inherited environment
      WorkDir       string                 // empty = per-test t.TempDir(); non-empty = use this directory for both binaries
      ExitCode      int                    // expected exit code for both binaries
      Normalize     []func([]byte) []byte  // applied in order to stdout and stderr of both binaries before comparison; nil or empty = no normalization
      ExpectedFiles map[string][]byte      // optional: path -> expected byte content after execution, for file-output utilities (sponge, cp)
  }

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text: DiffTest.Stdin nil means both binaries receive EOF immediately on stdin. An empty non-nil slice ([]byte{}) also produces no bytes but is semantically distinct (open stdin that is immediately closed).

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text:
DiffTest.Env nil means both binaries inherit the test process environment with
default overrides applied (see R2.6). When non-nil, the KEY=VALUE pairs in the
slice are merged into the inherited environment: matching keys are overridden, new
keys are added. This merge behavior matches the struct comment ("override or
extend") and avoids requiring callers to replicate the full environment for a
single override.

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text: Must define type NormalizeFunc = func([]byte) []byte as a named type alias in package testutils. The Normalize field in DiffTest uses this element type. When the slice is nil or empty, no normalization is applied to stdout or stderr.

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text: Must provide func RunDiffTests(t *testing.T, goBinary, refBinary string, tests []DiffTest) that accepts the path to the Go binary under test (goBinary) and the GNU reference binary (refBinary), then runs each DiffTest as a named subtest via t.Run(test.Name, ...). Both binaries are invoked with identical Args, Stdin, and Env for each test case.

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text: Must capture stdout, stderr, and exit code from each binary independently.

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text: Must impose a configurable timeout on each binary invocation. The default timeout must be 10 seconds. The test fails if either binary exceeds the timeout.

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text: Must not write any output to the test process stdout or stderr during a passing test run.

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text:
Must support passing a working directory to each binary invocation via a WorkDir
field on DiffTest. When WorkDir is empty, both binaries run in a per-test temporary
directory created by the harness via t.TempDir(). The harness must use the same
working directory for both binaries in a given test case. The DiffTest struct gains:

  WorkDir string // empty = per-test t.TempDir(); non-empty = use this directory for both binaries

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text:
Must set LC_ALL=C in the environment for both binaries unless the DiffTest.Env
explicitly overrides LC_ALL. This ensures deterministic sort order and formatting
across locales. The harness applies this default before merging DiffTest.Env.

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text: Must apply the DiffTest.Normalize function (if non-nil) to both binaries' stdout and stderr before comparison.

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text: Must compare normalized stdout byte-for-byte. Any difference must be reported as a test failure.

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text: Must compare normalized stderr byte-for-byte. Any difference must be reported as a test failure.

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text: Must compare exit codes exactly. A difference must be reported as a test failure.

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text: Must report divergence with the following information in the failure message: the DiffTest args, the stdin content (truncated to 256 bytes if longer), the reference binary stdout, the Go binary stdout, the reference stderr, the Go stderr, and both exit codes.

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text: Must run each DiffTest as a named subtest (t.Run) so individual test case failures are identifiable in go test output.

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text: Must allow per-DiffTest normalization via the Normalize field. The function receives the raw output bytes and returns the normalized bytes.

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text: Must provide a built-in TimestampNormalizer that replaces common strftime timestamp patterns with a fixed placeholder string. This normalizer is used by cmd/ts tests.

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text:
Must allow normalizers to be composed: the harness must accept a slice of Normalize
functions applied in order, not a single function. When the slice is nil or empty,
no normalization is applied.

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text:
Must provide func ComposeNormalizers(fns ...NormalizeFunc) NormalizeFunc that returns
a single NormalizeFunc applying the given functions in order. This is a convenience
for cmd/ test files that combine multiple normalizers:

  normalize := testutils.ComposeNormalizers(
      testutils.TimestampNormalizer,
      customNormalizer,
  )

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text:
Must support utilities whose primary output is a file rather than stdout (sponge,
cp, mv). DiffTest.ExpectedFiles is a map[string][]byte where keys are file paths
relative to the working directory and values are the expected byte content after
execution. When ExpectedFiles is non-nil, the harness checks each entry after both
binaries complete.

srd_title: pkg/testutils: Differential Testing Harness
req_text:
Must compare each ExpectedFiles entry byte-for-byte against the file produced by
the Go binary. Any difference must be reported as a test failure with the same
format as stdout divergence: file path, expected content (from reference), actual
content (from Go binary). Missing files must also be reported as failures.

srd_title: pkg/sys: Syscall Abstractions
req_text: Must provide func TerminalWidth() (int, error) that returns the current terminal column count by calling ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ) on stdout. Returns an error (not panic) when stdout is not a terminal or when ioctl fails.

srd_title: pkg/sys: Syscall Abstractions
req_text: Must use golang.org/x/sys/unix (the project's only external dependency) to perform the TIOCGWINSZ ioctl; must not shell out to tput or stty and must not import golang.org/x/term.

srd_title: pkg/sys: Syscall Abstractions
req_text:
Must provide func IsTerminal(fd uintptr) bool that returns true when the file
descriptor refers to a terminal, and false otherwise. Implementation: call
golang.org/x/sys/unix.IoctlGetWinsize(int(fd), unix.TIOCGWINSZ) and return
err == nil. Returns false for pipes, regular files, and non-terminal descriptors.
The caller (pkg/format ColorEnabled) is responsible for extracting the fd from an
io.Writer via type assertion to *os.File. Required by pkg/format to suppress color
output when stdout is redirected.

srd_title: pkg/sys: Syscall Abstractions
req_text: Utility context — ls (ls.c:2281): ls uses struct winsize to determine column count for its default multi-column layout and for the -w/--width flag default.

srd_title: pkg/sys: Syscall Abstractions
req_text:
Must provide func InstallSIGPIPEHandler() that installs a SIGPIPE handler causing the
process to exit 0 when stdout or stderr is closed by a downstream consumer.
Implementation: use signal.Notify(c, syscall.SIGPIPE) with a buffered channel of
size 1; in a dedicated goroutine call os.Exit(0) when the channel receives. Must not
use signal.Ignore so that deferred cleanup functions do not run on SIGPIPE (matching
GNU behavior where SIGPIPE terminates silently).

srd_title: pkg/sys: Syscall Abstractions
req_text: InstallSIGPIPEHandler must be safe to call multiple times; only one goroutine per invocation is started.

srd_title: pkg/sys: Syscall Abstractions
req_text: Utility context — ls (ls.c:1600-1620): ls installs a SIGPIPE handler via sigaction so that piping ls output to head does not produce a broken-pipe error message. du, find, and xargs have the same requirement.

srd_title: pkg/sys: Syscall Abstractions
req_text: Must provide func Stat(path string) (*FileInfo, error) and func Lstat(path string) (*FileInfo, error). Stat follows symbolic links (equivalent to os.Stat); Lstat does not follow symbolic links (equivalent to os.Lstat). Both return a *FileInfo populated from syscall.Stat_t.

srd_title: pkg/sys: Syscall Abstractions
req_text:
FileInfo must be defined as the following named struct in package sys:

  type FileInfo struct {
      Mode    os.FileMode // file mode and type bits (from syscall.Stat_t.Mode)
      Size    int64       // apparent file size in bytes (st_size)
      Nlink   uint64      // hard-link count (st_nlink)
      Uid     uint32      // owner user ID (st_uid)
      Gid     uint32      // owner group ID (st_gid)
      Rdev    uint64      // device ID for special files (st_rdev)
      Dev     uint64      // device ID of the containing filesystem (st_dev)
      Ino     uint64      // inode number (st_ino)
      Blocks  int64       // number of 512-byte blocks allocated (st_blocks)
      Blksize int64       // preferred I/O block size (st_blksize)
      ModTime time.Time   // modification time (st_mtime / st_mtimespec)
      Info    os.FileInfo // underlying os.FileInfo for os package compatibility
  }

srd_title: pkg/sys: Syscall Abstractions
req_text: Must abstract the Darwin/Linux divergence in struct field names (st_mtimespec on Darwin vs st_mtim on Linux; st_blocks interpretation) so callers use a single API regardless of target platform.

srd_title: pkg/sys: Syscall Abstractions
req_text: Utility context — ls (ls.c:213, 371): ls needs Nlink, Uid, Gid, Rdev, Mode for -l format; Blocks for -s; Ino for -i.

srd_title: pkg/sys: Syscall Abstractions
req_text: Utility context — du (du.c:554): du needs Dev and Ino for hard-link deduplication, and Blocks for physical block-count accumulation.

srd_title: pkg/sys: Syscall Abstractions
req_text: Utility context — find (find/ftsfind.c:172): find predicates (-type, -size, -newer, -perm, -uid, -gid) require Mode, Size, ModTime, Uid, Gid, Nlink from the stat struct.

srd_title: pkg/sys: Syscall Abstractions
req_text: Must provide func OnTerminalResize(callback func(width int)) that registers a SIGWINCH handler. When the terminal is resized, the handler calls TerminalWidth() and invokes the callback with the new width. If TerminalWidth() returns an error the callback is not invoked.

srd_title: pkg/sys: Syscall Abstractions
req_text: Must support multiple calls to OnTerminalResize; each registered callback must be called on resize. Callbacks are called in registration order.

srd_title: pkg/sys: Syscall Abstractions
req_text: Utility context — ls (ls.c:2281, SIGWINCH registration): ls re-queries terminal width on SIGWINCH to re-format output when the terminal window is resized during a long listing.

srd_title: pkg/format: Output Formatting
req_text: Must provide a Columns(entries []string, termWidth int) [][]string function that distributes entries into the maximum number of columns that fit within termWidth, using the longest entry in each column to determine column width.

srd_title: pkg/format: Output Formatting
req_text: Must provide a PadRight(s string, width int) string and PadLeft(s string, width int) string function for left- and right-aligned field padding within a fixed-width column.

srd_title: pkg/format: Output Formatting
req_text: Must treat multi-byte Unicode characters correctly: column width must be computed from display width (rune count via utf8.RuneCountInString), not byte count. East-asian full-width character handling is deferred; rune count is sufficient for ASCII-dominant utility output in the current roadmap.

srd_title: pkg/format: Output Formatting
req_text: Utility context — ls (ls.c multi-column layout): ls default output places filenames in as many columns as fit in the terminal width. Column widths are computed from the longest filename in each column, not the global maximum.

srd_title: pkg/format: Output Formatting
req_text: Must provide a FileTypeColor(mode os.FileMode) string function that returns the ANSI escape sequence for a file's type (directory, symlink, executable, block device, character device, socket, pipe, regular file).

srd_title: pkg/format: Output Formatting
req_text: Must provide a Reset() string constant or function that returns the ANSI reset sequence ("\033[0m").

srd_title: pkg/format: Output Formatting
req_text: Must provide a ColorEnabled(w io.Writer) bool function that returns true only when w is a TTY. Implementation: attempt a type assertion to *os.File; if it fails return false; call pkg/sys.IsTerminal(f.Fd()) which returns true when the file descriptor is a terminal (detected via TIOCGWINSZ ioctl), and false for pipes, regular files, and non-terminal descriptors. When ColorEnabled returns false, FileTypeColor must return an empty string and Reset must return an empty string.

srd_title: pkg/format: Output Formatting
req_text: Must use the same color assignments as GNU ls LS_COLORS defaults: directory=34 (blue), symlink=36 (cyan), executable=32 (green), block device=33;1 (yellow bold), character device=33;1 (yellow bold), socket=35 (magenta), pipe=33 (yellow), regular=0 (reset/default).

srd_title: pkg/format: Output Formatting
req_text: Utility context — ls (ls.c:103 includes dircolors.h, ls.c:273 get_color_indicator): ls outputs ANSI escapes before and after each filename in colorized mode. Color is suppressed when stdout is not a TTY or when --color=never is set.

srd_title: pkg/format: Output Formatting
req_text:
Must provide func SetColorEnabled(enabled bool) that overrides the automatic TTY
detection from ColorEnabled. When set to true, FileTypeColor and Reset return ANSI
sequences regardless of whether stdout is a TTY. When set to false, they return
empty strings regardless. This supports --color=always and --color=never flags in
utilities like ls. The override is process-global.

srd_title: pkg/format: Output Formatting
req_text:
Must provide func ResetColorEnabled() that clears any override set by
SetColorEnabled, reverting to automatic TTY detection via ColorEnabled. Utilities
must call ResetColorEnabled in deferred cleanup or test teardown to avoid leaking
the override across test cases.

srd_title: pkg/format: Output Formatting
pkg/format: Output Formatting
req_text: When opts.Binary is true (the default zero value), use base 1024 and suffixes []string{"", "K", "M", "G", "T", "P", "E"}. When opts.Binary is false, use base 1000 and suffixes []string{"", "kB", "MB", "GB", "TB"}.

srd_title: pkg/format: Output Formatting
req_text: Must format the output to at most one decimal place when the value is not an integer at the chosen unit (e.g., 1536 bytes must produce "1.5K", not "2K").

srd_title: pkg/format: Output Formatting
req_text: Must return "0" for a zero byte count regardless of the unit mode.

srd_title: pkg/format: Output Formatting
req_text: Utility context — ls (ls.c -h flag, human_output_opts): ls -h shows file sizes in human-readable form in -l output. The same conversion applies to ls -s (block counts).

srd_title: pkg/format: Output Formatting
req_text: Utility context — du (du.c:153 human_output_opts, du.c:442 human_readable()): du -h outputs directory sizes as human-readable strings. du uses the same binary/SI distinction as ls -h.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: Must read stdin line by line (newline-delimited). Each line must be written to stdout prefixed by a timestamp and a single space.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: The default timestamp format must be "%b %d %H:%M:%S" (strftime, e.g. "Feb 19 14:05:32"). The format must be evaluated at the time each line is received, not at startup.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: Must flush stdout after each line so that downstream consumers receive timestamps in real time.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: Must preserve the original newline at the end of each line; must not add an extra newline.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: Must pass through partial lines (lines not terminated by a newline at EOF) with a timestamp prefix.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: Exit code must be 0 after stdin is closed with EOF. Must not exit non-zero due to SIGPIPE when stdout is closed by a downstream consumer.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: Must accept an optional positional argument specifying a custom strftime format string, e.g. "ts '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S'".

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: Must support all standard strftime(3) conversion specifications available on the target platform.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: Must support three ts-specific subsecond extensions: %.S (seconds with microsecond suffix, e.g. "32.001234"), %.s (Unix epoch with microsecond suffix, e.g. "1708358732.001234"), %.T (HH:MM:SS with microsecond suffix, e.g. "14:05:32.001234"). These extensions require Time::HiRes in the Perl reference; the Go implementation must use time.Now() sub-nanosecond precision formatted to six decimal places.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: When a subsecond extension is used in the format string, must obtain both the second and microsecond components atomically from a single time sample per line.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: -i must change the timestamp to the time elapsed since the previous line was received. The first line's timestamp is the time elapsed since ts started.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: The default format in -i mode must be "%H:%M:%S". The TZ environment must be set to GMT so that strftime on a delta-second value produces a correct elapsed string (e.g., 5 seconds since last line → "00:00:05").

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: A custom format argument overrides the -i default format. The TZ=GMT behavior still applies.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: -i and -s are mutually exclusive; passing both must print a usage error to stderr and exit non-zero.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: -s must change the timestamp to the time elapsed since ts started, increasing monotonically across lines (unlike -i which resets per line).

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: The default format in -s mode must be "%H:%M:%S" with TZ=GMT, same as -i.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: A custom format argument overrides the -s default format.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: -m must use the system's monotonic clock (CLOCK_MONOTONIC via time.Now() in Go, which automatically uses the monotonic reading) instead of the wall clock for timestamp sampling.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: -m is compatible with all format modes (-i, -s, default) and with custom format strings including subsecond extensions.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: When -m is active, the timestamp must not jump backwards or exhibit discontinuities if the wall clock is adjusted (e.g., by NTP) while ts is running.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: -r must scan each input line for known timestamp patterns and replace each match with a human-readable relative age string (e.g., "15m5s ago").

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: Must recognize the following timestamp patterns from the Perl source regex: syslog format ("Jan  5 14:30:00"), ISO-8601 ("2024-01-05T14:30:00.000Z"), RFC 2822 with optional day ("16 Jun 94 07:29:35 GMT"), lastlog format ("Mon Jan  5 14:30").

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: When -r and a format string are both given, must convert matched timestamps to the specified format via strftime rather than to a relative string.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: Lines with no recognizable timestamp must be passed through unchanged.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: -r is mutually exclusive with -i and -s; passing both must print a usage error to stderr and exit non-zero.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: Must exit 0 on clean EOF from stdin.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: Must exit non-zero and print a usage message to stderr when an unrecognized flag is given.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: Must exit non-zero when -r mode is requested but the timestamp parsing dependency (equivalent of Date::Parse) is unavailable. In the Go implementation this means the parsing library must be compiled in, so this condition cannot arise; document the invariant in the implementation.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: Must respect the TZ environment variable to determine the local time zone for wall-clock timestamps (non -i/-s modes). Setting TZ=UTC must cause timestamps to be in UTC.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: In -i and -s modes, must use TZ=GMT internally for elapsed-time formatting regardless of the user's TZ setting, matching the Perl source behavior.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: Differential tests must use testutils.TimestampNormalizer (type func([]byte) []byte, defined in pkg/testutils) to replace wall-clock timestamps in output with a fixed placeholder before comparing Go and reference binary outputs. Pass it in the DiffTest.Normalize slice. The normalizer matches strftime-formatted patterns such as "Feb 19 14:05:32" and replaces them with a fixed string so that wall-clock differences do not cause test failures.

srd_title: cmd/ts: Timestamp Stdin Lines
req_text: Tests must cover: default format, custom strftime format, -s mode, -i mode, -m mode (with monotonic normalization), multi-line stdin, empty stdin, and partial last line (no trailing newline).

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: When no flags are given, must print line count, word count, and byte count (in that order) for each input, matching the wc.c default (print_lines = print_words = print_bytes = true; set at wc.c:862).

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: Must read from stdin when no file arguments are given. Must read from each named file in order when file arguments are given.

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: Output for each file must be on a single line with counts followed by the filename. For stdin input, no filename is printed.

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: When more than one file is given, must print a final "total" line with the sum of all counts.

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: -l must count newline characters (not logical lines). A file with no trailing newline has a newline count equal to the number of complete lines.

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: -w must count words, where a word is a maximal sequence of non-whitespace characters. Whitespace is determined by the locale-sensitive isspace() equivalent in Go (unicode.IsSpace).

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: -c must count bytes. -c and -m are mutually exclusive in output but may be passed together; -m takes precedence when both are given (matching wc.c behavior where print_chars overrides print_bytes display).

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: -m must count characters (Unicode code points), not bytes. When the input is valid UTF-8, this is the rune count. When the input contains invalid UTF-8, each invalid byte counts as one character.

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: -L must print the length of the longest line in the input, measured in display columns (tab-expanded, treating each tab as advancing to the next multiple of 8). -L is independent of other flags and may be combined with any of them.

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: When flags are combined, must print each requested count in the order: lines (-l), words (-w), chars (-m) or bytes (-c), max-line-length (-L). This is the fixed output column order from wc.c:237-247, not the flag order given by the user.

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: When multiple files are given, each line must right-align counts in columns wide enough for the largest count in that column across all files. This matches GNU wc's dynamic column-width behavior.

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: The total line must use the label "total" (not a filename). The counts in the total line must be the arithmetic sum of counts from all files.

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: Must support --total=auto (default), --total=always (print total even for one file), --total=only (print only the total, not per-file lines), and --total=never (never print total, even for multiple files).

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: Must treat "-" as a filename argument meaning stdin, consistent with POSIX convention.

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: Must handle binary input (arbitrary byte sequences) without corrupting output or panicking.

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: Must handle empty input (zero bytes) and produce "0 0 0" (or the selected subset of counts) correctly.

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: Must support --files0-from=FILE which reads NUL-delimited filenames from FILE and processes each. When FILE is "-", filenames are read from stdin.

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: Differential tests must set LC_ALL=C to avoid locale-dependent divergence between the Go and reference binary outputs for -m (character count). Document this constraint in the test suite.

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: Under LC_ALL=C, -m and -c must produce identical counts (each byte counts as one character). The Go implementation must produce the same result.

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: Must exit 0 when all inputs are processed successfully.

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: Must exit 1 when any input file cannot be opened or read. Must still process and print counts for the files that were successfully read before exiting 1.

srd_title: cmd/wc: Count Lines, Words, and Bytes
req_text: Must exit 1 when a write error occurs on stdout.

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: Must read each named file in argument order and write its contents verbatim to stdout.

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: Must read from stdin when no file arguments are given, or when "-" is given as a filename.

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: Must support concatenating multiple files: each file's content is written in sequence with no separator.

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: Must not corrupt binary input: output bytes must be identical to input bytes when no transformation flags are active.

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: Must not add or remove newlines from the input.

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: -n must prepend a line number to every output line. The line number must be right-justified in a field of width 6, followed by a tab character and then the line content (format: "%6d\t%s"). Line numbering resets to 1 at the start of each cat invocation, not per file.

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: -b must prepend a line number only to non-blank lines. Blank lines receive no number and no tab prefix. -b implies -n (activates line numbering) but overrides it by skipping blank lines.

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: When -b and -n are both given, -b takes precedence (blank lines are not numbered). This matches cat.c:602 where number_nonblank overrides number.

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: A blank line is a line containing only a newline character (zero non-newline bytes). Lines with spaces or tabs are not blank.

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: -s must suppress repeated blank lines: when two or more consecutive blank lines appear in the output, only one must be written. The first blank line is written; subsequent consecutive blank lines are discarded.

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: -s must apply across file boundaries when multiple files are concatenated: if the last line of file A and the first line of file B are both blank, they count as consecutive blank lines.

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: -s is compatible with -n and -b. When combined, squeezing is applied before numbering: the suppressed blank lines do not consume line numbers.

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: -v must display non-printing characters using caret notation and M- prefix. Control characters (0x00-0x1F except 0x09 tab and 0x0A newline) must be shown as ^X where X is the character 64 positions higher (e.g., 0x01 -> "^A", 0x1B -> "^["). Characters in the range 0x80-0x9F must be shown as "M-^X". Characters in the range 0xA0-0xFE must be shown as "M-X" where X is the character minus 0x80. The DEL character (0x7F) must be shown as "^?". 0xFF must be shown as "M-^?".

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: -v must not alter tab (0x09) or newline (0x0A) characters. Those are the two control characters exempted from -v display.

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: -E must append a "$" character before each newline in the output. The newline itself is still written after the "$".

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: -T must display tab characters (0x09) as the two-character sequence "^I" rather than the tab character itself.

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: -A is equivalent to -v -E -T combined. All three transformations are active simultaneously.

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: -e is equivalent to -v -E combined (show non-printing, show ends).

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: -t is equivalent to -v -T combined (show non-printing, show tabs).

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: -u is accepted but has no effect (cat.c:616: "we provide the -u feature unconditionally"). The flag must not produce an error.

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: Transformation flags are compatible with -n, -b, and -s. The order of application is: squeeze blanks (-s), then apply non-printing display (-v/-T), then append end-of-line marker (-E), then prepend line number (-n/-b).

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: Must exit 0 when all inputs are processed successfully.

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: Must exit 1 when any input file cannot be opened. The error message must be written to stderr. cat must continue processing remaining file arguments after the error.

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: Must exit 1 when a write error occurs on stdout (e.g., SIGPIPE or full disk). The write error must be detected and reported; the process must not hang.

srd_title: cmd/cat: Concatenate and Display Files
req_text: Must not exit non-zero due to SIGPIPE when stdout is closed by a downstream consumer. At startup, install a SIGPIPE handler: use signal.Notify(c, syscall.SIGPIPE) with a buffered channel of size 1; in a dedicated goroutine call os.Exit(0) when the channel receives. Do not use signal.Ignore (deferred cleanup functions must not run on SIGPIPE, matching GNU behavior).

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: Must read all bytes from stdin before opening or creating the output file. Opening the output file before stdin is closed violates the core contract and is not permitted.

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: Must buffer stdin in memory using a dynamically grown buffer starting at 8192 bytes, doubling on overflow, matching sponge.c:BUFF_SIZE and the realloc loop at sponge.c:313-324.

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: When the in-memory buffer would exceed the available memory threshold (derived from physmem_available() in the reference; in Go, use runtime.MemStats or a fixed fraction of RLIMIT_DATA), must spill the current buffer to a temp file and continue reading. The spill must be transparent: the final output is still a single concatenated byte stream.

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: Must create the temp file in the directory specified by the TMPDIR environment variable, or "/tmp" if TMPDIR is not set. The temp file name must follow the pattern "sponge.XXXXXX" (mkstemp-style random suffix).

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: Must register a cleanup handler (atexit equivalent in Go: defer or os/signal) that deletes the temp file if the process exits or receives SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP, or SIGPIPE before the rename completes.

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: When an output filename is given, must attempt an atomic rename of the temp file to the output filename when the output file is a regular file or does not yet exist (sponge.c:371-373).

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: When the rename fails (e.g., cross-device move), must fall back to a byte-for-byte copy of the temp file content to the output file, then delete the temp file.

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: When the output file already exists, must preserve its file mode (permissions) by reading the mode via lstat before writing and applying it to the output file via chmod (sponge.c:338-346). When the output file does not exist, must apply the default mode 0666 masked by the process umask.

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: Must use lstat (not stat) to check whether the output path exists and is a regular file (sponge.c:332-333). This matters when the output path is a symlink: sponge must replace the symlink target, not follow it blindly.

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: The output file must never be in a partially-written state observable by other processes. Either the rename succeeds atomically or the copy completes before the old file is removed.

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: -a must cause sponge to prepend the existing content of the output file to the stdin content before writing. The result is: [original file content][stdin content] written to the output file.

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: -a applies only when the output file already exists and is a regular file. When the output file does not exist, -a behaves identically to the default mode (creates a new file with stdin content).

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: The prepend operation must copy the original file content into the temp file first, then append the stdin buffer to the temp file (sponge.c:352-357). The original file must be read before the temp file is renamed over it.

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: When no output filename is given, must write the buffered stdin content to stdout after stdin is fully consumed.

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: In passthrough mode with large input (temp file spill), must seek the temp file to the beginning and copy its content to stdout (sponge.c:403-406).

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: In passthrough mode with small input (buffer fits in memory), must write the in-memory buffer directly to stdout without creating or reading a temp file (sponge.c:408-411).

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: Must exit 0 on success.

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: Must exit 1 when stdin cannot be read, when the temp file cannot be created or written, when the output file cannot be opened, or when the rename or copy fails. In all error cases, must print a descriptive error message to stderr via perror-equivalent before exiting.

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: Must exit 1 when memory allocation fails (buffer realloc). Must print an error and exit rather than panicking.

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: Must clean up the temp file on exit in all error paths. The temp file must not persist after the process exits, whether due to success or failure.

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: Differential tests must compare the content of the output file (not stdout) after both the Go binary and the reference binary have exited, using file-content comparison provided by pkg/testutils.

srd_title: cmd/sponge: Soak Stdin and Write to File
req_text: Tests must cover: small stdin (fits in memory), large stdin (forces temp file spill, tested with input larger than 1 MB), append mode, passthrough mode (no filename), output file does not exist, output file already exists (mode preservation), and the cross-device rename fallback (tested by placing the output file on a different filesystem from TMPDIR).

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: When stdout is a TTY and no format flag is given, must produce multi-column output sorted vertically (down columns, then across). Terminal width is obtained by calling pkg/sys.TerminalWidth() (int, error) — returns the current terminal column count via TIOCGWINSZ ioctl on stdout; returns an error when stdout is not a terminal. Entries are laid out by calling pkg/format.Columns(entries []string, termWidth int) [][]string — distributes entries into the maximum number of columns fitting within termWidth, with column widths computed as per-column maxima of entry lengths.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: When stdout is not a TTY (pipe, file redirect) and no format flag is given, must produce single-column output with one entry per line. This matches GNU ls behavior (ls.c detects stdout is not a TTY and sets format to single-column).

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: Must sort entries in the C locale order (LC_COLLATE=C). Differential tests must set LC_ALL=C to eliminate locale-dependent sort divergence.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: Must not list entries whose names start with "." unless -a or -A is given. This is the default filter behavior matching GNU ls.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -1 must produce single-column output with one entry per line regardless of whether stdout is a TTY. This overrides the default multi-column layout.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text:
-l flag skeleton and permission string. When -l is given, produce long-format output. Field order (left to right): permissions (10 chars), nlink, owner, group, size, mtime, name. Fields separated by a single space. Numeric fields (nlink, size) are right-aligned in columns wide enough for the largest value in the listing.

Permission string algorithm (10 characters):
- Position 0 (file type): 'd' for directory (fi.Mode&os.ModeDir != 0), 'l' for symlink (fi.Mode&os.ModeSymlink != 0), 'c' for char device (fi.Mode&os.ModeDevice != 0 && fi.Mode&os.ModeCharDevice != 0), 'b' for block device (fi.Mode&os.ModeDevice != 0 && fi.Mode&os.ModeCharDevice == 0), 'p' for FIFO (fi.Mode&os.ModeNamedPipe != 0), 's' for socket (fi.Mode&os.ModeSocket != 0), '-' for regular file.
- Positions 1-3 (owner rwx): 'r'/'- ' for bit 0o400, 'w'/'-' for 0o200, 'x'/'-' for 0o100. If setuid (fi.Mode&os.ModeSetuid != 0): replace 'x' with 's', or replace '-' with 'S'.
- Positions 4-6 (group rwx): bits 0o040, 0o020, 0o010. If setgid (fi.Mode&os.ModeSetgid != 0): replace 'x' with 's', or replace '-' with 'S'.
- Positions 7-9 (other rwx): bits 0o004, 0o002, 0o001. If sticky (fi.Mode&os.ModeSticky != 0): replace 'x' with 't', or replace '-' with 'T'.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text:
File metadata via pkg/sys.Lstat. Obtain metadata for each listed entry by calling pkg/sys.Lstat(path string) (*sys.FileInfo, error) — does not follow symbolic links; returns the symlink's own metadata when path is a symlink.

sys.FileInfo struct (embedded here for reference):
  type FileInfo struct {
      Mode    os.FileMode // file mode and type bits
      Size    int64       // apparent file size in bytes (st_size)
      Nlink   uint64      // hard-link count (st_nlink)
      Uid     uint32      // owner user ID (st_uid)
      Gid     uint32      // owner group ID (st_gid)
      Rdev    uint64      // device ID for special files (st_rdev)
      Dev     uint64      // device ID of the containing filesystem (st_dev)
      Ino     uint64      // inode number (st_ino)
      Blocks  int64       // number of 512-byte blocks allocated (st_blocks)
      Blksize int64       // preferred I/O block size (st_blksize)
      ModTime time.Time   // modification time
      Sys     os.FileInfo // underlying os.FileInfo
  }

In long format: print fi.Nlink (uint64) right-aligned; print fi.Size (int64, bytes) right-aligned. Both columns sized to the widest value across all listed entries.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: Owner and group name resolution in long format. Resolve owner name by calling os/user.LookupId(strconv.Itoa(int(fi.Uid))); on success use u.Username; on error (user not found or lookup fails) fall back to strconv.FormatUint(uint64(fi.Uid), 10). Resolve group name by calling os/user.LookupGroupId(strconv.Itoa(int(fi.Gid))); on success use g.Name; on error fall back to strconv.FormatUint(uint64(fi.Gid), 10). Owner and group fields are left-padded to column width for alignment.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: Modification time formatting in long format. Use fi.ModTime (time.Time from sys.FileInfo). If time.Since(fi.ModTime) < 6*30*24*time.Hour (approximately six months), format as fi.ModTime.Format("Jan _2 15:04"). Otherwise format as fi.ModTime.Format("Jan _2  2006"). Both patterns produce a 12-character field.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text:
Total block count line and symlink display. Before the directory listing, print "total N\n" where N = sum(fi.Blocks for all listed entries) / 2. The division converts 512-byte st_blocks units to 1K-block units matching GNU ls. N is a plain integer (no trailing suffix) unless -h is active (see R3).

Symlink display: when fi.Mode&os.ModeSymlink != 0, read the link target with os.Readlink(path) and append " -> " + target to the entry name field. Use Lstat (not Stat) so the symlink's own fi.Size and fi.Nlink are used, not the target's.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -C must force multi-column output regardless of whether stdout is a TTY. Layout uses pkg/format.Columns(entries []string, termWidth int) [][]string. When stdout is not a TTY, -C must use a default width of 80 columns (matching GNU ls behavior when stdout is not a TTY and -C is given without -w).

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -C must sort entries vertically (down columns, then across to the next column). This is the same sort direction as the default multi-column mode in R1.1.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -x must produce multi-column output with entries sorted horizontally (across columns, then down to the next row). This differs from -C which sorts vertically.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -C and -x are mutually exclusive with -l and -1. If -l or -1 appears after -C or -x on the command line, it overrides the multi-column mode. If -C or -x appears after -l or -1, it overrides the long or single-column format. The last format flag wins, matching GNU ls behavior.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -a must include entries whose names start with "." including the special entries "." and ".." in the listing.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -A must include entries whose names start with "." except for "." and "..". -A is the "almost all" filter.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -d must list directory entries themselves rather than their contents. When a directory is given as an argument with -d, must print the directory name (or its long-format entry with -l) without descending into it.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: When both -a and -A are given, the last one on the command line takes precedence, matching GNU ls behavior.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -t must sort entries by modification time, newest first. Obtain metadata via pkg/sys.Lstat(path string) (*sys.FileInfo, error); use sys.FileInfo.ModTime time.Time for comparison (fi.ModTime.After(fj.ModTime) for newest-first ordering). Entries with the same modification time must be sorted by name in C locale order as a tiebreaker.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -S must sort entries by file size (st_size), largest first. Obtain file size from sys.FileInfo.Size int64 — apparent file size in bytes (st_size). Entries with the same size must be sorted by name in C locale order as a tiebreaker.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -r must reverse the current sort order. -r applies to whichever sort is active (name sort by default, -t for time, -S for size, -v for version). -r with the default sort produces reverse alphabetical order.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -U must disable sorting entirely and list entries in directory order (the order returned by readdir). -U overrides -t, -S, and -v. -r with -U has no defined effect (directory order is not reversible in a meaningful way), but must be accepted without error.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -v must sort entries using natural version sort semantics (strverscmp behavior). Runs of digits within filenames are compared numerically rather than lexicographically, so "file2" sorts before "file10". Must be implemented without external libraries.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: When multiple sort flags are given, the last one on the command line takes precedence, matching GNU ls behavior.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -i must prepend the inode number of each entry before the entry name (or before the permissions in -l mode). Obtain the inode number via pkg/sys.Lstat(path string) (*sys.FileInfo, error) and read sys.FileInfo.Ino uint64 — inode number (st_ino). The inode number is right-aligned in a column wide enough for the largest inode in the listing.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -s must prepend the allocated block count for each entry before the entry name (or before the permissions in -l mode). Obtain the block count via pkg/sys.Lstat(path string) (*sys.FileInfo, error) and read sys.FileInfo.Blocks int64 — number of 512-byte blocks allocated (st_blocks). Report in 1024-byte block units: fi.Blocks / 2. The block count is right-aligned in a column wide enough for the largest count in the listing.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -s with -l must also modify the "total N" line to include block counts in the selected unit. The total is the sum of all listed entries' block allocations.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -n must activate long format (implies -l) and display numeric UID and GID instead of resolving owner and group names. Format UID as strconv.FormatUint(uint64(fi.Uid), 10) and GID as strconv.FormatUint(uint64(fi.Gid), 10), where fi.Uid uint32 and fi.Gid uint32 come from pkg/sys.Lstat. Do not call os/user.LookupId or os/user.LookupGroupId.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -i and -s may be combined. When both are given, inode is printed first, then block count, then the entry (or the long-format fields).

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: Must support --color=always, --color=auto, and --color=never. When --color is given without a value, it must default to "always".

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: --color=auto must colorize output only when stdout is a TTY. TTY detection: call pkg/sys.IsTerminal(os.Stdout) — returns true when os.Stdout's file descriptor is a terminal (detected via golang.org/x/sys/unix.IoctlGetWinsize with TIOCGWINSZ), false otherwise. When stdout is not a TTY, --color=auto must behave like --color=never.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text:
Colorized output uses GNU LS_COLORS default color assignments via pkg/format. Call pkg/format.FileTypeColor(mode os.FileMode) string to obtain the ANSI escape sequence for a given file type, and pkg/format.Reset() string for the reset sequence. Executable detection: fi.Mode&0o111 != 0 (any execute bit set). Each entry name is wrapped as: colorCode + name + resetCode. When color is suppressed, both codes are empty strings so no ANSI sequences appear in output.

Set the process-global color mode based on the --color flag value: call pkg/format.SetColorEnabled(true) for --color=always, pkg/format.SetColorEnabled(false) for --color=never. For --color=auto, call pkg/sys.IsTerminal(os.Stdout.Fd()) and pass the result to pkg/format.SetColorEnabled. When color is disabled, pkg/format.FileTypeColor returns empty strings.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: When --color=never or when color is suppressed (non-TTY with auto), must not emit any ANSI escape sequences in the output.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -h must only take effect with -l (long format). When -h is given with -l, file sizes (fi.Size int64) must be displayed via pkg/format.HumanSize(bytes int64, opts HumanSizeOpts) string with opts.Binary = true (1024-base units, suffixes K/M/G/T/P/E). Without -l, -h must have no visible effect on output.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -h must also apply to the "total N" block count line in long format. When -h is active, convert the total block count (sum(fi.Blocks)/2 as int64) to a human-readable string using the same binary algorithm before printing "total X\n".

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text:
-h must apply to -s block counts when both -s and -h are given, converting
block counts to human-readable form. Use pkg/format.HumanSize(bytes int64,
opts HumanSizeOpts) string with opts.Binary = true, consistent with R3.5.
Do not duplicate the HumanSize algorithm inline.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -F must append a type indicator character after each entry name. The indicators are "/" for directories, "*" for executable regular files, "@" for symbolic links, "|" for named pipes (FIFOs), "=" for sockets. Regular non-executable files receive no indicator.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: Executable is defined as having any execute bit set (owner, group, or other) in the file's permission mode.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -F must work with all output formats (-l, -1, -C, -x) and with color output. When color is enabled, the indicator character is printed after the ANSI reset sequence so it is not colorized.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -R must recursively list the contents of each subdirectory encountered during the listing. Each subdirectory's contents are printed under a header line in the format "PATH:" followed by a blank line, then the directory contents, then a blank line before the next entry.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -R must respect the current format mode. With -l, each subdirectory's contents are listed in long format including the "total N" block line. With -C or default mode, each subdirectory's contents use multi-column layout.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -R must not follow symbolic links to directories. Only real subdirectories are recursed into.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -R must apply the current filter flags (-a, -A) to each subdirectory. Dotfiles in subdirectories are shown only if -a or -A is given.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -R must list directories in the same sort order as entries within a directory. If -t is active, subdirectories are recursed into in modification-time order.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: Must exit 0 when all listed paths are accessed and output is written successfully.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: Must exit 1 when a minor problem occurs, such as failing to access a file or directory given as an argument (e.g., permission denied, file not found). Must still list the remaining accessible entries before exiting. Must print a diagnostic to stderr for each inaccessible entry.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: Must exit 2 when a serious problem occurs, such as an invalid command-line option. This matches GNU ls (ls.c:5638 exit(status) where status is set to EXIT_FAILURE=2 for bad options at ls.c:2026).

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: Must install a SIGPIPE handler at startup so that piping ls output to head or other truncating consumers does not produce a broken-pipe error message. Implementation: call pkg/sys.InstallSIGPIPEHandler() — this uses signal.Notify(c, syscall.SIGPIPE) with a buffered channel of size 1; a dedicated goroutine calls os.Exit(0) when the channel receives. Must not use signal.Ignore (deferred cleanup functions must not run on SIGPIPE, matching GNU ls behavior).

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: Must install a SIGWINCH handler via pkg/sys.OnTerminalResize(callback func(width int)) that re-queries the terminal width and updates the column layout. pkg/sys.OnTerminalResize registers a SIGWINCH listener that calls pkg/sys.TerminalWidth() and invokes the callback with the new width; multiple callbacks may be registered. This allows ls to adapt column layout if the terminal is resized during a long listing.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -n implies -l. When -n is given without -l, the output must be in long format with numeric UID/GID.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -C and -x are mutually exclusive with -l and -1. The last format flag on the command line wins (see R1.14).

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -R with -l must produce a "total N" block line for each subdirectory listing, matching GNU ls -lR output.

srd_title: cmd/ls: File Listing
req_text: -i, -s, and -F may all be combined with -R. Each subdirectory listing applies the same metadata display and classification options.

srd_title: cmd/du: Recursive Directory Disk Usage
req_text: Must recurse into each directory argument and print the accumulated size and path for each subdirectory and the directory itself. When no arguments are given, must default to the current directory (".").

srd_title: cmd/du: Recursive Directory Disk Usage
req_text:
Must report sizes in 1024-byte (1K) block units by default. Each entry's size is fi.Blocks / 2 where fi.Blocks (int64) is the number of 512-byte blocks allocated (st_blocks from syscall.Stat_t). Obtain metadata via pkg/sys.Stat(path string) (*sys.FileInfo, error) — follows symbolic links. sys.FileInfo.Blocks int64 holds the 512-byte block count.

sys.FileInfo struct (embedded for reference):
  type FileInfo struct {
      Mode    os.FileMode
      Size    int64       // apparent file size in bytes (st_size)
      Nlink   uint64      // hard-link count (st_nlink)
      Uid     uint32      // owner user ID (st_uid)
      Gid     uint32      // owner group ID (st_gid)
      Rdev    uint64      // device ID for special files (st_rdev)
      Dev     uint64      // device ID of the containing filesystem (st_dev)
      Ino     uint64      // inode number (st_ino)
      Blocks  int64       // 512-byte blocks allocated (st_blocks)
      Blksize int64       // preferred I/O block size
      ModTime time.Time   // modification time
      Sys     os.FileInfo // underlying os.FileInfo
  }

srd_title: cmd/du: Recursive Directory Disk Usage
req_text: Must print one line per entry in the format "SIZE\tPATH\n" where SIZE is a right-aligned integer (no leading spaces) and PATH is the relative path as given by the directory traversal.

srd_title: cmd/du: Recursive Directory Disk Usage

srd_title: cmd/du: Recursive Directory Disk Usage
req_text: Hard-link deduplication applies per du invocation, not per argument. A hard-linked file counted under one argument must not be counted again under a subsequent argument.

srd_title: cmd/du: Recursive Directory Disk Usage
req_text: Must exit 0 when all arguments are traversed and reported successfully.

srd_title: cmd/du: Recursive Directory Disk Usage
req_text: Must exit 1 when any error occurs during traversal (cannot stat a file, cannot read a directory, permission denied). Must print a diagnostic to stderr for each error and continue processing remaining entries and arguments before exiting.

srd_title: cmd/tac: Concatenate and Print Files in Reverse

Must treat a trailing separator at the end of input as the terminator of the last record, not as a separator before an empty record. This matches gtac behavior where "a
b
" reversed produces "b
a
" not "

srd_title: cmd/tac: Concatenate and Print Files in Reverse
req_text: Must read from stdin when no file arguments are given, or when "-" appears as a filename.

srd_title: cmd/tac: Concatenate and Print Files in Reverse
req_text: When multiple files are given, must process each file independently and write them in argument order (each file's records reversed, files not merged before reversal).

srd_title: cmd/tac: Concatenate and Print Files in Reverse
req_text: -s SEP must use SEP as the record separator instead of newline. SEP may be any string.

srd_title: cmd/tac: Concatenate and Print Files in Reverse
req_text: By default the separator follows each record. -b must place the separator before each record instead of after it.

srd_title: cmd/tac: Concatenate and Print Files in Reverse
req_text: -r must interpret the -s SEP argument as a regular expression (Go regexp syntax). Each match of the pattern becomes a record boundary.

srd_title: cmd/tac: Concatenate and Print Files in Reverse
req_text: When -s and -r are combined, the separator is a regex; records are the text between consecutive matches.

srd_title: cmd/nl: Number Lines of Files
req_text: By default, must number non-empty lines in the body section only, using right-justified numbers in a field of width 6, with a tab character separating the number from the line content.

srd_title: cmd/nl: Number Lines of Files
req_text: Empty lines (containing only a newline) in the body section must not be numbered by default. They must be passed through with no number and no separator.

srd_title: cmd/nl: Number Lines of Files
req_text: Must read from stdin when no file arguments are given. Must read each named file in argument order.

srd_title: cmd/nl: Number Lines of Files
req_text: Line numbering must be continuous across files when multiple files are given (the counter does not reset between files unless a page delimiter is encountered).

srd_title: cmd/nl: Number Lines of Files
req_text: -b STYLE must set the body section numbering style. Styles: a (number all lines), t (number non-empty lines, default), n (number no lines), p RE (number lines matching regular expression RE).

srd_title: cmd/nl: Number Lines of Files
req_text: -h STYLE must set the header section numbering style (default n). Same style values as -b.

srd_title: cmd/nl: Number Lines of Files
req_text: -f STYLE must set the footer section numbering style (default n). Same style values as -b.

srd_title: cmd/nl: Number Lines of Files
req_text: When the style is n for a section, lines in that section must pass through with no number and no separator character.

srd_title: cmd/nl: Number Lines of Files
req_text: -n FORMAT must set the line number format. Formats: ln (left-justified, no leading zeros), rn (right-justified, no leading zeros, default), rz (right-justified, leading zeros).

srd_title: cmd/nl: Number Lines of Files
req_text: -w N must set the line number field width to N characters (default 6).

srd_title: cmd/nl: Number Lines of Files
req_text: -s SEP must use SEP as the separator between the line number and the line content (default tab). SEP may be any string.

srd_title: cmd/nl: Number Lines of Files
req_text: -v N must set the initial line number to N (default 1). -i N must set the line number increment to N (default 1).

srd_title: cmd/nl: Number Lines of Files
req_text: A line containing only the two-character sequence \:\:\: (the section delimiter repeated three times) marks the start of a header section. \:\: marks the start of a body section. \: marks the start of a footer section. These delimiter lines are not written to output.

srd_title: cmd/nl: Number Lines of Files
req_text: Each new logical page (triggered by a header delimiter) resets the line counter to the value of -v unless -p is given.

srd_title: cmd/nl: Number Lines of Files
req_text: -p must suppress line counter reset at the start of each logical page; numbering continues from the previous page's last line number.

srd_title: cmd/nl: Number Lines of Files
req_text: -l N must treat N consecutive empty lines as a single empty line for the purpose of numbering with -b t. The default is 1 (each empty line counted separately). With -l 2, two or fewer consecutive empty lines are treated as one unnumbered block.

srd_title: cmd/fold: Wrap Long Lines to a Specified Width
req_text: Must read each file (or stdin when no arguments are given) and write each line wrapped to at most W characters (columns by default, bytes with -b). The default width is 80.

srd_title: cmd/fold: Wrap Long Lines to a Specified Width
req_text: Lines shorter than or equal to the maximum width must be written unchanged (including the trailing newline).

srd_title: cmd/fold: Wrap Long Lines to a Specified Width
req_text: Lines longer than the maximum width must be split by inserting a newline after exactly W columns (or bytes with -b). Wrapping is applied repeatedly until the remaining portion fits within the width.

srd_title: cmd/fold: Wrap Long Lines to a Specified Width
req_text: The final segment of a wrapped line retains the original newline if the source line ended with one; a line without a trailing newline produces a final segment without one.

srd_title: cmd/fold: Wrap Long Lines to a Specified Width
req_text: -w N must set the maximum line width to N. N must be a positive integer. If N is 0 or negative, fold must exit with an error message to stderr and exit code 1.

srd_title: cmd/fold: Wrap Long Lines to a Specified Width
req_text: By default, width is measured in display columns. Tab characters count as the number of columns needed to reach the next tab stop (tab stops every 8 columns). Other control characters count as one column.

srd_title: cmd/fold: Wrap Long Lines to a Specified Width
req_text: -b must measure width in bytes rather than columns. Each byte counts as 1 regardless of whether it is a tab or multi-byte character. This disables tab-stop expansion for width measurement.

srd_title: cmd/fold: Wrap Long Lines to a Specified Width
req_text: -s must break lines at the last space character at or before the wrap column, rather than at an exact column position.

srd_title: cmd/fold: Wrap Long Lines to a Specified Width
req_text: If no space character appears within the first W columns of a segment, -s must fall back to breaking at exactly W columns (same behavior as without -s).

srd_title: cmd/fold: Wrap Long Lines to a Specified Width
req_text: The space character at the break point is written as the last character of the current output line before the inserted newline. The next line starts with the character immediately following the space.

srd_title: cmd/fold: Wrap Long Lines to a Specified Width
req_text: -s is compatible with -b; space detection uses byte positions when -b is active.

srd_title: cmd/fold: Wrap Long Lines to a Specified Width
req_text: Must exit 0 when all inputs are processed successfully.

srd_title: cmd/fold: Wrap Long Lines to a Specified Width
req_text: Must exit 1 when any input file cannot be opened, printing the error to stderr. Processing continues for remaining files.

srd_title: cmd/fold: Wrap Long Lines to a Specified Width
req_text: Must exit 1 when a write error occurs on stdout.

srd_title: cmd/fold: Wrap Long Lines to a Specified Width

srd_title: cmd/expand: Convert Tabs to Spaces
req_text: By default, tab characters must be replaced by enough spaces to advance to the next multiple-of-8 column position. Column positions are 1-indexed; a tab at column 1 advances to column 9.

srd_title: cmd/expand: Convert Tabs to Spaces
req_text: Multiple consecutive tabs must each advance to the next tab stop independently.

srd_title: cmd/expand: Convert Tabs to Spaces
req_text: Non-tab characters must be written unchanged. Each non-tab byte (including multi-byte UTF-8 sequences under LC_ALL=C) counts as one column.

srd_title: cmd/expand: Convert Tabs to Spaces
req_text: Newline characters reset the column position to 1 for the next line.

srd_title: cmd/expand: Convert Tabs to Spaces
req_text: -t N must set a uniform tab stop interval of N columns (equivalent to tab stops at N, 2N, 3N, ...). N must be a positive integer.

srd_title: cmd/expand: Convert Tabs to Spaces
req_text: -t LIST must set tab stops at the absolute column positions given in LIST (comma-separated or space-separated positive integers in strictly increasing order). A tab at or past the last explicit tab stop is replaced by a single space.

srd_title: cmd/expand: Convert Tabs to Spaces
req_text: The -t option replaces the default tab stop interval of 8. If -t is given multiple times, the last value takes effect.

srd_title: cmd/expand: Convert Tabs to Spaces
req_text: When LIST contains a single value, it behaves identically to -t N (uniform interval).

srd_title: cmd/expand: Convert Tabs to Spaces
req_text: Must exit 0 when all inputs are processed successfully.

srd_title: cmd/expand: Convert Tabs to Spaces
req_text: Must exit 1 when any input file cannot be opened, printing the error to stderr. Processing continues for remaining files.

srd_title: cmd/expand: Convert Tabs to Spaces
req_text: Must exit 1 when a write error occurs on stdout.

srd_title: cmd/expand: Convert Tabs to Spaces
req_text: Must handle SIGPIPE gracefully (exit 0) using pkg/sys.InstallSIGPIPEHandler.

srd_title: cmd/expand: Convert Tabs to Spaces
req_text: Differential tests must compare Go expand output against gexpand byte-for-byte via pkg/testutils.RunDiffTests.

srd_title: cmd/expand: Convert Tabs to Spaces
req_text: Tests must cover: default tab expansion, -t N with a single interval, -t LIST with multiple tab stops, input with no tabs (passthrough), and multiple tabs in succession.

srd_title: cmd/expand: Convert Tabs to Spaces
req_text: Tests must use LC_ALL=C to eliminate locale-dependent divergence.

srd_title: cmd/unexpand: Convert Spaces to Tabs
req_text: By default, unexpand must replace leading spaces (and mixed leading spaces and tabs) with tabs only when doing so advances to the same column position. Tabs are preferred over spaces when a run of spaces reaches a tab stop exactly.

srd_title: cmd/unexpand: Convert Spaces to Tabs
req_text: Non-leading whitespace must be written unchanged in default mode. Characters after the first non-whitespace character on a line are not converted.

srd_title: cmd/unexpand: Convert Spaces to Tabs
req_text: A run of spaces that does not exactly reach a tab stop must be kept as spaces; unexpand must not insert a tab that would overshoot the column.

srd_title: cmd/unexpand: Convert Spaces to Tabs
req_text: Existing tab characters in leading whitespace count toward the column position as in expand; they do not prevent further tab substitution.

srd_title: cmd/unexpand: Convert Spaces to Tabs
req_text: -a must convert all runs of spaces (not just leading) where replacement with tabs aligns to a tab stop. The rule is the same as R1.1 applied at every column position in the line, not only at the start.

srd_title: cmd/unexpand: Convert Spaces to Tabs
req_text: A single space that does not reach a tab stop must be kept as a space even with -a.

srd_title: cmd/unexpand: Convert Spaces to Tabs
req_text: The first non-space, non-tab character on the line does not stop the conversion; -a processes the entire line.

srd_title: cmd/unexpand: Convert Spaces to Tabs
req_text: -t N must set a uniform tab stop interval of N columns. -t LIST must set absolute tab stop positions. Behavior mirrors srd024-expand R2.1 and R2.2 for tab stop resolution.

srd_title: cmd/unexpand: Convert Spaces to Tabs
req_text: When past the last explicit tab stop in a LIST, remaining spaces are kept as-is (no tab can be inserted beyond the last defined stop).

srd_title: cmd/unexpand: Convert Spaces to Tabs
req_text: -t implies -a; when custom tab stops are given, all whitespace in the line is subject to conversion, not just leading whitespace.

srd_title: cmd/unexpand: Convert Spaces to Tabs
req_text: Must exit 0 when all inputs are processed successfully.

srd_title: cmd/unexpand: Convert Spaces to Tabs
req_text: Must exit 1 when any input file cannot be opened, printing the error to stderr. Processing continues for remaining files.

srd_title: cmd/unexpand: Convert Spaces to Tabs
req_text: Must exit 1 when a write error occurs on stdout.

srd_title: cmd/cut: Remove Sections from Lines
req_text: -b LIST must extract the specified byte positions from each line. LIST is a comma-separated list of ranges; each range is N, N-M, N- (from N to end), or -M (from start to M). Bytes are 1-indexed.

srd_title: cmd/cut: Remove Sections from Lines
req_text: -c LIST must extract the specified character positions. Under LC_ALL=C, -c and -b are equivalent (one byte per character). The flag is provided for compatibility.

srd_title: cmd/cut: Remove Sections from Lines
req_text: With -b or -c, newline characters are not counted as part of the line; they are passed through to terminate each output line.

srd_title: cmd/cut: Remove Sections from Lines
req_text: Lines shorter than the selected range produce no bytes for the out-of-range positions; only the bytes that exist are output.

srd_title: cmd/cut: Remove Sections from Lines
req_text: -f LIST must extract the specified fields from each line, where fields are delimited by the character given with -d (default tab). LIST uses the same range syntax as -b.

srd_title: cmd/cut: Remove Sections from Lines
req_text: -d DELIM must set the input field delimiter to the single character DELIM. The delimiter must be exactly one byte. When the output delimiter is not explicitly set with --output-delimiter, the input delimiter is also used as the output delimiter.

srd_title: cmd/cut: Remove Sections from Lines
req_text: -s must suppress lines that do not contain the delimiter. Without -s, lines with no delimiter are printed unchanged.

srd_title: cmd/cut: Remove Sections from Lines
req_text: --output-delimiter STRING must use STRING as the separator between selected output fields, replacing the default (which is the input delimiter).

srd_title: cmd/cut: Remove Sections from Lines
req_text: --complement must invert the selection; the output contains the bytes, characters, or fields NOT specified by the range list.

srd_title: cmd/cut: Remove Sections from Lines
req_text: --complement is compatible with -b, -c, and -f. It is not compatible with -s.

srd_title: cmd/cut: Remove Sections from Lines
req_text: With --complement and -f, fields not in the list are output in their original order, separated by the output delimiter.

srd_title: cmd/cut: Remove Sections from Lines
req_text: Must exit 0 when all inputs are processed successfully.

srd_title: cmd/cut: Remove Sections from Lines
req_text: Must exit 1 when any input file cannot be opened, printing the error to stderr. Processing continues for remaining files.

srd_title: cmd/cut: Remove Sections from Lines
req_text: Must exit 1 when a write error occurs on stdout.

srd_title: cmd/cut: Remove Sections from Lines
req_text: Must handle SIGPIPE gracefully (exit 0) using pkg/sys.InstallSIGPIPEHandler.

srd_title: cmd/paste: Merge Lines of Files Side by Side
req_text: Must open all named files simultaneously and read one line from each per output line. Lines from files are joined with the delimiter and written to stdout, followed by a newline.

srd_title: cmd/paste: Merge Lines of Files Side by Side
req_text: When files have unequal line counts, the shorter files contribute empty fields (the delimiter is still written) until all files are exhausted. The final output line ends with a newline.

srd_title: cmd/paste: Merge Lines of Files Side by Side
req_text: stdin is used as an input when "-" is given as a filename. Multiple "-" arguments each refer to stdin read sequentially.

srd_title: cmd/paste: Merge Lines of Files Side by Side
req_text: When no files are given, must read from stdin and write each line followed by a newline (passthrough behavior matching gpaste with a single stdin source).

srd_title: cmd/paste: Merge Lines of Files Side by Side
req_text: -d DELIM must use DELIM as the separator between fields. DELIM may be a single character or a list; if a list is given, the delimiters are cycled in order across the fields of each output line.

srd_title: cmd/paste: Merge Lines of Files Side by Side
req_text: The escape sequences \\n (newline), \\t (tab), \\\\ (backslash), and \\0 (empty string, no delimiter) are recognized in DELIM.

srd_title: cmd/paste: Merge Lines of Files Side by Side
req_text: When DELIM cycles back to the start for a new output line, cycling resets from the first delimiter in the list.

srd_title: cmd/paste: Merge Lines of Files Side by Side
req_text: -s must process files one at a time. All lines of the first file are joined with the delimiter and written as a single output line. Then all lines of the second file are written as a single output line, and so on.

srd_title: cmd/paste: Merge Lines of Files Side by Side
req_text: In serial mode, the delimiter list cycles across fields within the single output line for each file. The trailing newline is always written.

srd_title: cmd/paste: Merge Lines of Files Side by Side
req_text: -s and the default parallel mode are mutually exclusive; -s overrides parallel mode.

srd_title: cmd/paste: Merge Lines of Files Side by Side

srd_title: cmd/uniq: Report or Filter Adjacent Duplicate Lines
req_text: By default, must read each line and write it once, suppressing all but the first occurrence of any run of identical adjacent lines.

srd_title: cmd/uniq: Report or Filter Adjacent Duplicate Lines
req_text: Lines that appear only once must be written. Lines that appear multiple times in a run must be written once. Non-adjacent duplicates are unaffected (uniq does not sort input).

srd_title: cmd/uniq: Report or Filter Adjacent Duplicate Lines
req_text: Must read from stdin when no file argument is given. Must accept an optional output file as a second argument.

srd_title: cmd/uniq: Report or Filter Adjacent Duplicate Lines
req_text: Comparison is case-sensitive by default. Each line includes the newline terminator in the comparison.

srd_title: cmd/uniq: Report or Filter Adjacent Duplicate Lines
req_text: -d must print only lines that appear more than once in a run (one copy per run). Lines that appear only once are suppressed.

srd_title: cmd/uniq: Report or Filter Adjacent Duplicate Lines
req_text: -D must print all lines of each run that appears more than once. Every copy of a duplicated run is written, not just the first.

srd_title: cmd/uniq: Report or Filter Adjacent Duplicate Lines
req_text: -u must print only lines that appear exactly once (runs of one).

srd_title: cmd/uniq: Report or Filter Adjacent Duplicate Lines
req_text: -c must prefix each output line with the count of occurrences in its run, right-justified in a field wide enough to hold the count, followed by a space and the line.

srd_title: cmd/uniq: Report or Filter Adjacent Duplicate Lines
req_text: -i must perform case-insensitive comparison. Lines that differ only in case are treated as duplicates.

srd_title: cmd/uniq: Report or Filter Adjacent Duplicate Lines
req_text: -f N must skip the first N fields (whitespace-separated tokens) of each line before comparing. The skipped fields are still written to output.

srd_title: cmd/uniq: Report or Filter Adjacent Duplicate Lines
req_text: -s N must skip the first N characters of each line before comparing. The skipped characters are still written to output.

srd_title: cmd/uniq: Report or Filter Adjacent Duplicate Lines
req_text: -w N must compare only the first N characters of each line (after -f and -s adjustments). Characters beyond N are ignored for comparison purposes but still written.

srd_title: cmd/uniq: Report or Filter Adjacent Duplicate Lines
req_text: Must exit 0 when all inputs are processed successfully.
