srd_title: cmd/comm: Compare Two Sorted Files Line by Line
req_text: Must read file1 and file2 simultaneously, line by line. Lines present only in file1 are written in column 1 (no indentation). Lines present only in file2 are written in column 2 (one tab indent). Lines present in both are written in column 3 (two tabs indent).

srd_title: cmd/comm: Compare Two Sorted Files Line by Line
req_text: Must process files in sorted order; when a line from file1 is lexicographically less than the current file2 line, it is a column-1 line. When file2's line is less, it is a column-2 line. Equal lines go to column 3.

srd_title: cmd/comm: Compare Two Sorted Files Line by Line
req_text: When one file is exhausted, all remaining lines from the other file go to the appropriate column (column 1 if file1 has lines left, column 2 if file2 has lines left).

srd_title: cmd/comm: Compare Two Sorted Files Line by Line
req_text: Comparison is byte-for-byte with LC_ALL=C (no locale collation). An optional newline at the end of the last line does not affect comparison.

srd_title: cmd/comm: Compare Two Sorted Files Line by Line
req_text: -1 must suppress column 1 (lines unique to file1). The remaining columns shift left in indentation.

srd_title: cmd/comm: Compare Two Sorted Files Line by Line
req_text: -2 must suppress column 2 (lines unique to file2). The remaining columns shift left accordingly.

srd_title: cmd/comm: Compare Two Sorted Files Line by Line
req_text: -3 must suppress column 3 (lines common to both files). Combining -1 -2 -3 produces no output.

srd_title: cmd/comm: Compare Two Sorted Files Line by Line
req_text: When a column is suppressed, the tab indentation for remaining columns adjusts so that the leftmost output column has no leading tab.

srd_title: cmd/comm: Compare Two Sorted Files Line by Line
req_text: By default, comm checks that input files are sorted. When a line is encountered that is less than the previous line in the same file, comm prints a warning to stderr and continues.

srd_title: cmd/comm: Compare Two Sorted Files Line by Line
req_text: --check-order makes the ordering check fatal; comm exits non-zero if input is not sorted.

srd_title: cmd/comm: Compare Two Sorted Files Line by Line
req_text: --nocheck-order disables the sorting check entirely; no warning is printed even if input is out of order.

srd_title: cmd/comm: Compare Two Sorted Files Line by Line
req_text: --output-delimiter=STRING replaces the default tab character as the column separator. All column indentation levels use STRING instead of a tab.

srd_title: cmd/comm: Compare Two Sorted Files Line by Line
req_text: Must exit 0 when all inputs are processed successfully and no order violations occur.

srd_title: cmd/comm: Compare Two Sorted Files Line by Line
req_text: Must exit 1 when any input file cannot be opened, printing the error to stderr.

req_text: Must exit 1 when a write error occurs on stdout.

srd_title: cmd/md5sum: Compute and Check MD5 Message Digests
req_text: Must read from stdin and print "HASH  -" when no file arguments are given or when "-" is provided as a filename.

srd_title: cmd/md5sum: Compute and Check MD5 Message Digests
req_text: --tag must use BSD-style output format "MD5 (FILENAME) = HASH" instead of the default GNU format.

srd_title: cmd/md5sum: Compute and Check MD5 Message Digests
req_text: Must exit 1 when any named file cannot be opened, printing an error to stderr, and continue processing remaining files.

srd_title: cmd/md5sum: Compute and Check MD5 Message Digests
req_text: --check FILE must read FILE line by line, parsing lines in GNU format (HASH  FILENAME or HASH *FILENAME) or BSD tag format, compute the digest for each named file, and compare it to the stored hash.

srd_title: cmd/md5sum: Compute and Check MD5 Message Digests
req_text: For each verified file, must print "FILENAME: OK" or "FILENAME: FAILED" to stdout. After processing all entries, if any failed, must exit 1.

srd_title: cmd/md5sum: Compute and Check MD5 Message Digests
req_text: --warn (-w) must print a warning to stderr for each improperly formatted line in the checksum file; without --warn, malformed lines are silently skipped.

srd_title: cmd/md5sum: Compute and Check MD5 Message Digests
req_text: --quiet suppresses the "OK" lines; only failures are printed. --status suppresses all output; exit code conveys success/failure.

srd_title: cmd/md5sum: Compute and Check MD5 Message Digests
req_text: -b (--binary) marks the input as binary; the output line uses one space followed by an asterisk before the filename ("HASH *FILENAME"). On Linux/macOS there is no functional difference between binary and text mode for digest computation.

srd_title: cmd/md5sum: Compute and Check MD5 Message Digests
req_text: -t (--text) is the default; the output line uses two spaces before the filename ("HASH  FILENAME").

srd_title: cmd/md5sum: Compute and Check MD5 Message Digests
req_text: When --tag is given with -b, the output is BSD tag format; the mode flag has no effect on the tag format.

srd_title: cmd/md5sum: Compute and Check MD5 Message Digests
req_text: Must exit 0 when all files are processed and all verified digests match.

srd_title: cmd/md5sum: Compute and Check MD5 Message Digests
req_text: Must exit 1 when any file cannot be opened, any digest fails verification, or the checksum file is unreadable.

srd_title: cmd/md5sum: Compute and Check MD5 Message Digests
req_text: Must handle SIGPIPE gracefully (exit 0) using pkg/sys.InstallSIGPIPEHandler.

srd_title: cmd/sha1sum: Compute and Check SHA-1 Message Digests
req_text: Must compute the SHA-1 digest of each named file and write one line per file in the format "HASH  FILENAME" (text mode) or "HASH *FILENAME" (binary mode). The default is text mode.

srd_title: cmd/mv: Move or Rename Files
req_text: When the destination cannot be overwritten due to permissions, must print an error to stderr.

srd_title: cmd/mv: Move or Rename Files
req_text: -v or --verbose must print the name of each file as it is moved, in the format 'SOURCE -> DEST' or 'renamed SOURCE -> DEST'.

srd_title: cmd/mv: Move or Rename Files
req_text: -t DIRECTORY or --target-directory=DIRECTORY must move all SOURCE arguments into DIRECTORY.

srd_title: cmd/mv: Move or Rename Files
req_text: -T or --no-target-directory must treat DEST as a normal file, not a directory.

srd_title: cmd/mv: Move or Rename Files
req_text: Must exit 0 when all files are moved successfully.

srd_title: cmd/mv: Move or Rename Files
req_text: Must exit 1 when any move operation fails (permission denied, source not found).

srd_title: cmd/mv: Move or Rename Files
req_text: When moving multiple files and one fails, must continue moving remaining files and exit 1.

srd_title: cmd/mv: Move or Rename Files
req_text: Differential tests must compare exit codes and resulting file system state between the Go binary and the reference binary via pkg/testutils. srd_title: cmd/rm: Remove Files or Directories
req_text: When given one or more FILE arguments, must remove each file using unlink(2).

srd_title: cmd/rm: Remove Files or Directories
req_text: Without -r, must refuse to remove a directory and print an error to stderr.

srd_title: cmd/rm: Remove Files or Directories
req_text: Must not remove '.' or '..' to prevent accidental directory tree destruction. Must print an error if either is specified.

srd_title: cmd/rm: Remove Files or Directories
req_text: When a file cannot be removed (permission denied, in use), must print an error to stderr and continue with remaining files.

srd_title: cmd/rm: Remove Files or Directories
req_text: -r or -R or --recursive must remove directories and their contents recursively.

srd_title: cmd/rm: Remove Files or Directories
req_text: -f or --force must ignore non-existent files and never prompt. Overrides -i and -I.

srd_title: cmd/rm: Remove Files or Directories
req_text: When -r and -f are combined, must silently remove directory trees without prompting.

srd_title: cmd/rm: Remove Files or Directories
req_text: -d or --dir must remove empty directories. Without -d or -r, directory removal fails.

srd_title: cmd/rm: Remove Files or Directories
req_text: -i must prompt before every removal.

srd_title: cmd/rm: Remove Files or Directories
req_text: -I must prompt once before removing more than three files or when removing recursively.

srd_title: cmd/rm: Remove Files or Directories
req_text: -v or --verbose must print the name of each file as it is removed.

srd_title: cmd/rm: Remove Files or Directories
req_text: --interactive=WHEN must control prompting. WHEN is 'never' (like -f), 'once' (like -I), or 'always' (like -i).

srd_title: cmd/rm: Remove Files or Directories
req_text: Must exit 0 when all files are removed successfully.

srd_title: cmd/rm: Remove Files or Directories
req_text: Must exit 1 when any removal fails. Must continue removing remaining files.

srd_title: cmd/rm: Remove Files or Directories
req_text: With -f, must exit 0 even when specified files do not exist.

srd_title: cmd/rm: Remove Files or Directories
req_text: Differential tests must compare exit codes and resulting file system state between the Go binary and the reference binary via pkg/testutils. Tests must cover: single file removal, multi-file removal, -r recursive, -f force on non-existent, -d empty directory, -v verbose, error on directory without -r, error on permission denied, and refusing to remove '.' or '..'.

srd_title: cmd/version: Version Identity Binary
req_text:
Must provide a cmd/version/ package that compiles to a standalone binary. When
invoked with no arguments, the binary prints the version string to stdout followed
by a newline and exits 0.

srd_title: cmd/version: Version Identity Binary
req_text:
The version string must be set at build time via -ldflags "-X main.version=<tag>".
When the linker variable is not set (development builds), the binary must print
"dev" as the version string.

srd_title: cmd/version: Version Identity Binary
req_text:
The mage build target must resolve the version tag by running
git describe --tags --abbrev=0 --match "v[0-9]*" and passing the result to the
linker. If the git command fails (no tags, not a git repository), the build must
succeed with the version set to "dev".

srd_title: cmd/version: Version Identity Binary
req_text:
When invoked with --version or -v, the binary must print the same version string
as the no-argument invocation. Any other flag must cause the binary to print a
usage message to stderr and exit 2.

srd_title: cmd/version: Version Identity Binary
req_text:
The version package must export a variable or function so that other cmd/ packages
can import and report the same version string without duplicating the ldflags
mechanism.

srd_title: cmd/date: Display and Format Date and Time
req_text: When invoked with no arguments, must print the current date and time in the default format and exit 0.

srd_title: cmd/date: Display and Format Date and Time
req_text: When a +FORMAT argument is given, must format the date according to the strftime-style format string and print the result followed by a newline.

srd_title: cmd/date: Display and Format Date and Time
req_text: Must support all standard strftime conversion specifications including %Y (year), %m (month), %d (day), %H (hour), %M (minute), %S (second), %Z (timezone name), %s (seconds since epoch), %N (nanoseconds), %A (weekday name), %B (month name), %j (day of year), %u (day of week 1-7), and %w (day of week 0-6).

srd_title: cmd/date: Display and Format Date and Time
req_text: Must support GNU extensions including %P (lowercase am/pm) and padding modifiers (%-d for no padding, %_d for space padding, %0d for zero padding).

srd_title: cmd/date: Display and Format Date and Time
req_text: -d STRING or --date=STRING must display the date described by STRING instead of the current time.

srd_title: cmd/date: Display and Format Date and Time
req_text: Must parse epoch timestamps prefixed with @ (e.g., -d @1234567890).

srd_title: cmd/date: Display and Format Date and Time
req_text: Must parse ISO 8601 date strings (e.g., -d '2024-01-15 10:30:00').

srd_title: cmd/date: Display and Format Date and Time
req_text: When the date string cannot be parsed, must print an error to stderr and exit 1.

srd_title: cmd/date: Display and Format Date and Time
req_text: -u or --utc or --universal must display the date in UTC instead of the local timezone.

srd_title: cmd/date: Display and Format Date and Time
req_text: -r FILE or --reference=FILE must display the last modification time of FILE instead of the current time.

srd_title: cmd/date: Display and Format Date and Time
req_text: When the referenced file does not exist, must print an error to stderr and exit 1.

srd_title: cmd/date: Display and Format Date and Time
req_text: Must not read from stdin. Must write formatted output to stdout only.

srd_title: cmd/date: Display and Format Date and Time
req_text: Must exit 0 when the date is displayed successfully.

srd_title: cmd/date: Display and Format Date and Time
req_text: Must exit 1 when an invalid date string is given or a referenced file does not exist.

srd_title: cmd/date: Display and Format Date and Time
req_text: Differential tests must compare stdout and exit codes between the Go binary and the reference binary via pkg/testutils. Tests must use fixed dates via -d @EPOCH to ensure deterministic output.

srd_title: cmd/date: Display and Format Date and Time
req_text: Tests must cover: default output with fixed epoch, +FORMAT with various conversion specs, -d with epoch and ISO strings, -u UTC mode, -r reference file, padding modifiers, and error cases (invalid date, missing file).

srd_title: cmd/sleep: Pause for a Specified Duration
req_text: Must pause for NUMBER seconds when given a single numeric argument, then exit 0.

srd_title: cmd/sleep: Pause for a Specified Duration
req_text: Must support fractional seconds (e.g., sleep 0.5 pauses for 500 milliseconds).

srd_title: cmd/sleep: Pause for a Specified Duration
req_text: Must support suffix multipliers s (seconds, default), m (minutes, x60), h (hours, x3600), d (days, x86400). The suffix is case-sensitive and lowercase only.

srd_title: cmd/sleep: Pause for a Specified Duration
req_text: When multiple arguments are given, must sum all durations and sleep for the total.

srd_title: cmd/sleep: Pause for a Specified Duration
req_text: Must accept zero as a valid duration and return immediately with exit 0.

srd_title: cmd/sleep: Pause for a Specified Duration
req_text: When no arguments are given, must print a usage error to stderr and exit 1.

srd_title: cmd/sleep: Pause for a Specified Duration
req_text: When a non-numeric or negative argument is given, must print an error to stderr and exit 1.

srd_title: cmd/sleep: Pause for a Specified Duration
req_text: Must support infinity (or inf) as a duration, sleeping indefinitely until interrupted.

srd_title: cmd/sleep: Pause for a Specified Duration
req_text: Must not produce any output to stdout or stderr under normal operation.

srd_title: cmd/sleep: Pause for a Specified Duration
req_text: Must not read from stdin.

srd_title: cmd/sleep: Pause for a Specified Duration
req_text: When --help is the first argument, must print a usage message to stdout and exit 0.

srd_title: cmd/sleep: Pause for a Specified Duration
req_text: When --version is the first argument, must print version information to stdout and exit 0.

srd_title: cmd/sleep: Pause for a Specified Duration
req_text: Must exit 0 after sleeping for the requested duration.

srd_title: cmd/sleep: Pause for a Specified Duration
req_text: Must exit 1 when given invalid arguments (no args, non-numeric, negative).

srd_title: cmd/sleep: Pause for a Specified Duration
req_text: Differential tests must compare exit codes between the Go binary and the reference binary via pkg/testutils. Tests must use short durations (0 or 0.01) to avoid slow test execution.

srd_title: cmd/sleep: Pause for a Specified Duration
req_text: Tests must cover: zero duration, fractional seconds, suffix multipliers (s, m, h, d), multiple arguments summed, error on no args, error on invalid arg, and error on negative arg.

srd_title: cmd/touch: Create Files and Update Timestamps
req_text: When given one or more FILE arguments, must update the access and modification times of each file to the current time.

srd_title: cmd/touch: Create Files and Update Timestamps
req_text: When a named file does not exist, must create it as an empty file with default permissions.

srd_title: cmd/touch: Create Files and Update Timestamps
req_text: -c or --no-create must suppress file creation. If the file does not exist, must not create it and must not report an error.

srd_title: cmd/touch: Create Files and Update Timestamps
req_text: Must support multiple file arguments, processing each in order.

srd_title: cmd/touch: Create Files and Update Timestamps
req_text: -a must change only the access time.

srd_title: cmd/touch: Create Files and Update Timestamps
req_text: -m must change only the modification time.

srd_title: cmd/touch: Create Files and Update Timestamps
req_text: When neither -a nor -m is given, must change both access and modification times.

srd_title: cmd/touch: Create Files and Update Timestamps
req_text: -t STAMP must use the timestamp [[CC]YY]MMDDhhmm[.ss] instead of the current time.

srd_title: cmd/touch: Create Files and Update Timestamps
req_text: -r FILE or --reference=FILE must use the timestamps of FILE instead of the current time.

srd_title: cmd/touch: Create Files and Update Timestamps
req_text: -d STRING or --date=STRING must parse the date string and use it instead of the current time.

srd_title: cmd/touch: Create Files and Update Timestamps
req_text: When a reference file does not exist, must print an error to stderr and exit 1.

srd_title: cmd/touch: Create Files and Update Timestamps
req_text: -h or --no-dereference must affect the symbolic link itself rather than the file it points to.

srd_title: cmd/touch: Create Files and Update Timestamps
req_text: Must exit 0 when all files are processed successfully.

srd_title: cmd/touch: Create Files and Update Timestamps
req_text: Must exit 1 when an error occurs (invalid timestamp, missing reference file, permission denied). Must continue processing remaining files after an error.

srd_title: cmd/touch: Create Files and Update Timestamps
req_text: Differential tests must compare exit codes and resulting file timestamps between the Go binary and the reference binary via pkg/testutils.

srd_title: cmd/touch: Create Files and Update Timestamps
req_text: Tests must cover: create new file, update existing file, -c no-create, -a access only, -m modification only, -t explicit timestamp, -d date string, -r reference file, multiple files, and error cases (invalid timestamp, missing reference file).

srd_title: cmd/timeout: Run a Command with a Time Limit
req_text: Must run COMMAND with optional ARGS and kill it with SIGTERM if it does not exit within DURATION seconds.

srd_title: cmd/timeout: Run a Command with a Time Limit
req_text: Must support fractional durations (e.g., timeout 0.5 command).

srd_title: cmd/timeout: Run a Command with a Time Limit
req_text: Must support suffix multipliers s (seconds, default), m (minutes), h (hours), d (days).

srd_title: cmd/timeout: Run a Command with a Time Limit
req_text: When DURATION is 0, must not impose a time limit (the command runs indefinitely).

srd_title: cmd/timeout: Run a Command with a Time Limit
req_text: -s SIGNAL or --signal=SIGNAL must send the specified signal instead of SIGTERM. Must accept signal names (e.g., KILL, HUP) and numeric signal values.

srd_title: cmd/timeout: Run a Command with a Time Limit
req_text: -k DURATION or --kill-after=DURATION must send SIGKILL if the command is still running DURATION seconds after the initial signal.

srd_title: cmd/timeout: Run a Command with a Time Limit
req_text: --foreground must not create a separate process group, allowing the command to use the terminal.

srd_title: cmd/timeout: Run a Command with a Time Limit
req_text: --preserve-status must exit with the same status as the command, even on timeout, instead of the timeout-specific exit code 124.

srd_title: cmd/timeout: Run a Command with a Time Limit
req_text: When the command exits before the timeout, must exit with the command's exit status.

srd_title: cmd/timeout: Run a Command with a Time Limit
req_text: When the command is killed due to timeout, must exit 124 (unless --preserve-status is given).

srd_title: cmd/timeout: Run a Command with a Time Limit
req_text: When the command is killed by a signal not sent by timeout, must exit 128+signum.

srd_title: cmd/timeout: Run a Command with a Time Limit
req_text: When the timeout command itself fails (invalid arguments, command not found), must exit 125 for internal error or 126/127 for command execution failure.

srd_title: cmd/timeout: Run a Command with a Time Limit
req_text: Differential tests must compare exit codes between the Go binary and the reference binary via pkg/testutils.

srd_title: cmd/timeout: Run a Command with a Time Limit
req_text: Tests must cover: command completes before timeout (exit with command status), command exceeds timeout (exit 124), duration 0 (no limit), -s with named and numeric signals, -k kill-after escalation, --preserve-status, and error cases (no args, invalid duration, command not found).

srd_title: cmd/timeout: Run a Command with a Time Limit
req_text: Tests must use fast commands (true, false, sleep 0) and short durations to avoid slow test execution.

srd_title: cmd/timeout: Run a Command with a Time Limit
req_text: Tests must verify that the timed-out process is actually killed and does not remain as an orphan.

srd_title: cmd/shuf: Shuffle Lines Randomly
req_text: When given one or more FILE arguments, must read all lines from each file, randomly permute them, and write the result to stdout.

srd_title: cmd/shuf: Shuffle Lines Randomly
req_text: When no file arguments are given or when "-" is given as a filename, must read from stdin.

srd_title: cmd/shuf: Shuffle Lines Randomly
req_text: Must output each input line exactly once in a random order (a permutation, not sampling with replacement) unless -r is given.

srd_title: cmd/shuf: Shuffle Lines Randomly
req_text: Must treat each line as terminated by a newline. The last line need not end with a newline, but must be included in the shuffle.

srd_title: cmd/shuf: Shuffle Lines Randomly
req_text: -i LO-HI or --input-range=LO-HI must generate and shuffle integers from LO to HI inclusive, one per line. Must not be combined with file arguments.

srd_title: cmd/shuf: Shuffle Lines Randomly
req_text: -n COUNT or --head-count=COUNT must output at most COUNT lines.

srd_title: cmd/shuf: Shuffle Lines Randomly
req_text: -r or --repeat must allow output lines to repeat (sampling with replacement). Without -n, runs indefinitely.

srd_title: cmd/shuf: Shuffle Lines Randomly
req_text: -o FILE or --output=FILE must write output to FILE instead of stdout.

srd_title: cmd/shuf: Shuffle Lines Randomly
req_text: --random-source=FILE must read random bytes from FILE instead of the system random source.

srd_title: cmd/shuf: Shuffle Lines Randomly
req_text: -z or --zero-terminated must use NUL (\0) as the line delimiter instead of newline, for both input and output.

srd_title: cmd/shuf: Shuffle Lines Randomly
req_text: -e or --echo must treat each ARG as an input line instead of reading from files.

srd_title: cmd/shuf: Shuffle Lines Randomly
req_text: Must handle empty input (zero lines) by producing no output and exiting 0.

srd_title: cmd/shuf: Shuffle Lines Randomly
req_text: Must exit 0 on successful operation.

srd_title: cmd/shuf: Shuffle Lines Randomly
req_text: Must exit 1 on error (invalid range, conflicting options, write error).

srd_title: cmd/shuf: Shuffle Lines Randomly
req_text: Differential tests must verify structural properties rather than exact output: correct line count, values within range for -i, no duplicates without -r, duplicates allowed with -r.

srd_title: cmd/shuf: Shuffle Lines Randomly
req_text: Tests must cover: shuffle stdin lines, shuffle file lines, -i range mode, -n head count, -r repeat mode, -e echo mode, -z zero-terminated, empty input, and error cases (invalid range, -i with files).

srd_title: cmd/factor: Prime Factorization
req_text: For each integer argument, must print a line in the format 'NUMBER: FACTOR FACTOR ...' where factors are in ascending order with repetition for multiplicity (e.g., '12: 2 2 3').

srd_title: cmd/factor: Prime Factorization
req_text: For the number 1, must print '1:' with no factors.

srd_title: cmd/factor: Prime Factorization
req_text: Must handle prime numbers by printing the number itself as the sole factor.

srd_title: cmd/factor: Prime Factorization
req_text: Must process multiple arguments in order, printing one factorization line per argument.

srd_title: cmd/factor: Prime Factorization
req_text: When no arguments are given, must read integers from stdin, one per line, and factorize each.

srd_title: cmd/factor: Prime Factorization
req_text: Must accept integers up to at least 2^63-1 (the Go int64 maximum).

srd_title: cmd/factor: Prime Factorization
req_text: Must skip blank lines in stdin mode without producing output or error.

srd_title: cmd/factor: Prime Factorization
req_text: When a non-integer or negative input is encountered, must print an error to stderr and continue processing remaining inputs.

srd_title: cmd/factor: Prime Factorization
req_text: When --help is the first argument, must print a usage message to stdout and exit 0.

srd_title: cmd/factor: Prime Factorization
req_text: When --version is the first argument, must print version information to stdout and exit 0.

srd_title: cmd/factor: Prime Factorization
req_text: Must write factorization output to stdout, one line per integer.

srd_title: cmd/factor: Prime Factorization
req_text: Must write error messages to stderr without stopping processing of remaining inputs.

srd_title: cmd/factor: Prime Factorization
req_text: Must exit 0 when all inputs are valid and factorized successfully.

srd_title: cmd/factor: Prime Factorization
req_text: Must exit 1 when any input is invalid (non-integer, negative, overflow).

srd_title: cmd/factor: Prime Factorization
req_text: Differential tests must compare stdout and exit codes between the Go binary and the reference binary via pkg/testutils.

srd_title: cmd/factor: Prime Factorization
req_text: Tests must cover: single number, multiple numbers, primes, composites, 1, large numbers, stdin mode, error on non-integer, and error on negative number.

srd_title: cmd/expr: Evaluate Expressions
req_text: Must support integer arithmetic operators: + (add), - (subtract), * (multiply), / (integer divide), % (modulo). Each operator and operand is a separate argument.

srd_title: cmd/expr: Evaluate Expressions
req_text: Must support comparison operators: < (less), <= (less-equal), = (equal), != (not-equal), >= (greater-equal), > (greater). Comparisons on two integers use numeric comparison; otherwise use lexicographic comparison. Must return 1 for true and 0 for false.

srd_title: cmd/expr: Evaluate Expressions
req_text: Must support logical operators: | (or) returns the first argument if it is nonzero/non-empty, else the second; & (and) returns the first argument if both are nonzero/non-empty, else 0.

srd_title: cmd/expr: Evaluate Expressions
req_text: Must support parentheses for grouping: ( and ) override default precedence. Parentheses are separate arguments.

srd_title: cmd/expr: Evaluate Expressions
req_text: match STRING REGEXP or STRING : REGEXP must anchor the pattern at the beginning of STRING and return the matched substring if the pattern contains \( \), or the number of matched characters otherwise.

srd_title: cmd/expr: Evaluate Expressions
req_text: substr STRING POS LENGTH must return a substring of STRING starting at position POS (1-based) with length LENGTH.

srd_title: cmd/expr: Evaluate Expressions
req_text: index STRING CHARS must return the position (1-based) of the first character in STRING that is also in CHARS, or 0 if none.

srd_title: cmd/expr: Evaluate Expressions
req_text: length STRING must return the number of characters in STRING.

srd_title: cmd/expr: Evaluate Expressions
req_text: + TOKEN must interpret TOKEN as a string even if it is a keyword (match, substr, index, length) or operator. The + is consumed and not part of the value.

srd_title: cmd/expr: Evaluate Expressions
req_text: Operator precedence from lowest to highest: | , & , comparisons (< <= = != >= >), + - (arithmetic), * / %.

srd_title: cmd/expr: Evaluate Expressions
req_text: All binary operators are left-associative.

srd_title: cmd/expr: Evaluate Expressions
req_text: Division by zero must print an error to stderr and exit 2.

srd_title: cmd/expr: Evaluate Expressions
req_text: Must exit 0 when the expression evaluates to a non-null, non-zero value.

srd_title: cmd/expr: Evaluate Expressions
req_text: Must exit 1 when the expression evaluates to null or 0.

srd_title: cmd/expr: Evaluate Expressions
req_text: Must exit 2 on syntax error (invalid expression, missing operand, division by zero). Must exit 3 on internal error.

srd_title: cmd/expr: Evaluate Expressions
req_text: Differential tests must compare stdout, stderr emptiness, and exit codes between the Go binary and the reference binary via pkg/testutils. Tests must cover: integer arithmetic (all operators), comparisons (numeric and string), logical operators, string operations (match, substr, index, length), parentheses, + escaping, division by zero, and missing operand errors.

srd_title: cmd/split: Split a File into Pieces
req_text: When invoked with no options, must split the input into pieces of 1000 lines each, writing to files named xaa, xab, xac, etc.

srd_title: cmd/split: Split a File into Pieces
req_text: When a PREFIX argument is given, must use PREFIX instead of 'x' as the output filename prefix.

srd_title: cmd/split: Split a File into Pieces
req_text: -l N or --lines=N must split the input into pieces of N lines each.

srd_title: cmd/split: Split a File into Pieces
req_text: When reading from stdin or when FILE is "-", must read from stdin.

srd_title: cmd/split: Split a File into Pieces
req_text: -b N or --bytes=N must split the input into pieces of N bytes each. N may have a suffix (K, M, G, T, P, E, Z, Y for powers of 1024, or KB, MB, etc. for powers of 1000).

srd_title: cmd/split: Split a File into Pieces
req_text: -C N or --line-bytes=N must split the input into pieces of at most N bytes each, breaking only at line boundaries. Lines longer than N bytes are written to their own piece.

srd_title: cmd/split: Split a File into Pieces
req_text: -n CHUNKS or --number=CHUNKS must split the input into CHUNKS pieces of roughly equal size. Must support N (by bytes), l/N (by lines), and r/N (round-robin by lines) forms.

srd_title: cmd/split: Split a File into Pieces
req_text: Must not split in more than one mode simultaneously; conflicting split options must produce an error and exit 1.

srd_title: cmd/split: Split a File into Pieces
req_text: -a N or --suffix-length=N must use suffixes of length N (default 2).

srd_title: cmd/split: Split a File into Pieces
req_text: -d or --numeric-suffixes must use numeric suffixes (00, 01, 02, ...) instead of alphabetic.

srd_title: cmd/split: Split a File into Pieces
req_text: --additional-suffix=SUFFIX must append SUFFIX to each output filename after the alphabetic or numeric suffix.

srd_title: cmd/split: Split a File into Pieces
req_text: --filter=COMMAND must write each piece to the given shell COMMAND via a pipe, with the output filename available as $FILE in the command.

srd_title: cmd/split: Split a File into Pieces
req_text: Must exit 0 when the input is split successfully.

srd_title: cmd/split: Split a File into Pieces
req_text: Must exit 1 when an invalid option, conflicting options, or write error occurs.

srd_title: cmd/split: Split a File into Pieces
req_text: Differential tests must compare output file contents and exit codes between the Go binary and the reference binary via pkg/testutils.

srd_title: cmd/split: Split a File into Pieces
req_text: Tests must cover: default 1000-line split, -l with custom line count, -b byte split with and without suffixes, -C line-bytes, -n chunk modes, -a suffix length, -d numeric suffixes, --additional-suffix, stdin input, custom prefix, and error cases (conflicting options, invalid counts).

srd_title: cmd/csplit: Split a File into Context-Determined Pieces
req_text: Must accept one or more PATTERN arguments. Each pattern is applied in order to split the input at the matching boundary.

srd_title: cmd/csplit: Split a File into Context-Determined Pieces
req_text: /REGEXP/ must split at the next line matching REGEXP. The matching line becomes the first line of the next piece.

srd_title: cmd/csplit: Split a File into Context-Determined Pieces
req_text: %REGEXP% must skip to the next line matching REGEXP without creating an output file for the skipped content.

srd_title: cmd/csplit: Split a File into Context-Determined Pieces
req_text: INTEGER must split at the given line number. The specified line becomes the first line of the next piece.

srd_title: cmd/csplit: Split a File into Context-Determined Pieces
req_text: {N} appended to a pattern must repeat that pattern N additional times (total N+1 applications).

srd_title: cmd/csplit: Split a File into Context-Determined Pieces
req_text: {*} appended to a pattern must repeat that pattern as many times as possible until end of input.

srd_title: cmd/csplit: Split a File into Context-Determined Pieces
req_text: /REGEXP/+N and /REGEXP/-N must split N lines after or before the matching line, respectively.

srd_title: cmd/csplit: Split a File into Context-Determined Pieces
req_text: When a pattern does not match, must print an error to stderr. With --suppress-matched this is not an error if at least one split occurred.

srd_title: cmd/csplit: Split a File into Context-Determined Pieces
req_text: Must write output files named xx00, xx01, xx02, etc. by default.

srd_title: cmd/csplit: Split a File into Context-Determined Pieces
req_text: -f PREFIX or --prefix=PREFIX must use PREFIX instead of 'xx' for output filenames.

srd_title: cmd/csplit: Split a File into Context-Determined Pieces
req_text: -n DIGITS or --digits=DIGITS must use DIGITS-wide numeric suffixes (default 2).

srd_title: cmd/csplit: Split a File into Context-Determined Pieces
req_text: -z or --elide-empty-files must suppress creation of empty output files.

srd_title: cmd/csplit: Split a File into Context-Determined Pieces
req_text: Must exit 0 when the input is split successfully.

srd_title: cmd/csplit: Split a File into Context-Determined Pieces
req_text: Must exit 1 when a pattern fails to match (unless suppressed) or an invalid option is given.

srd_title: cmd/csplit: Split a File into Context-Determined Pieces
req_text: Differential tests must compare output file contents and exit codes between the Go binary and the reference binary via pkg/testutils.

srd_title: cmd/csplit: Split a File into Context-Determined Pieces
req_text: Tests must cover: regex split, line number split, skip patterns (%), repeat counts ({N} and {*}), offset (+N/-N), -f custom prefix, -n digit width, -z elide empty, stdin input, and error cases (no match, invalid regex).

srd_title: cmd/join: Join Lines of Two Files on a Common Field
req_text: Must read two sorted files and join lines where the join field (default: first field) matches. Must print one output line per matching pair.

srd_title: cmd/join: Join Lines of Two Files on a Common Field
req_text: Fields in each line are separated by whitespace (runs of blanks and tabs) by default. The output separator is a single space by default.

srd_title: cmd/join: Join Lines of Two Files on a Common Field
req_text: Lines that do not pair (present in one file but not the other) are suppressed by default.

srd_title: cmd/join: Join Lines of Two Files on a Common Field
req_text: When one of the file arguments is '-', must read that file from stdin.

srd_title: cmd/join: Join Lines of Two Files on a Common Field
req_text: -1 FIELD must join on field FIELD of file 1 (fields are numbered from 1). -2 FIELD must join on field FIELD of file 2.

srd_title: cmd/join: Join Lines of Two Files on a Common Field
req_text: -j FIELD must set the join field for both files simultaneously.

srd_title: cmd/join: Join Lines of Two Files on a Common Field
req_text: -o FORMAT must select and order output fields. FORMAT is a comma-separated or space-separated list of FILENUM.FIELDNUM specifiers (e.g., 1.2,2.1) or '0' for the join field.

srd_title: cmd/join: Join Lines of Two Files on a Common Field
req_text: -t CHAR must use CHAR as both the input and output field separator.

srd_title: cmd/join: Join Lines of Two Files on a Common Field
req_text: -a FILENUM must also print unpairable lines from file FILENUM (1 or 2). May be specified twice (-a 1 -a 2) to print unpairable lines from both files.

srd_title: cmd/join: Join Lines of Two Files on a Common Field
req_text: -v FILENUM must print only unpairable lines from file FILENUM, suppressing paired lines.

srd_title: cmd/join: Join Lines of Two Files on a Common Field
req_text: -e STRING must replace missing input fields with STRING in the output.

srd_title: cmd/join: Join Lines of Two Files on a Common Field
req_text: --header must treat the first line of each input file as a header line, joining them regardless of sort order and printing the result before data lines.

srd_title: cmd/join: Join Lines of Two Files on a Common Field
req_text: Must exit 0 when the join completes successfully.

srd_title: cmd/join: Join Lines of Two Files on a Common Field
req_text: Must exit 1 when an invalid option is given or a file cannot be opened.

srd_title: cmd/join: Join Lines of Two Files on a Common Field
req_text: Differential tests must compare stdout and exit codes between the Go binary and the reference binary via pkg/testutils. Tests must use LC_ALL=C for deterministic collation.

srd_title: cmd/join: Join Lines of Two Files on a Common Field
req_text: Tests must cover: default join on first field, -1/-2 field selection, -j combined field, -t custom separator, -o output format, -a unpairable lines, -v unpairable only, -e empty replacement, --header, stdin as one input, and error cases (unsorted input with --check-order, missing file).

srd_title: cmd/fmt: Simple Text Formatter
req_text: When invoked with no options, must reformat each paragraph of input text to fit within 75 characters (the GNU default width).

srd_title: cmd/fmt: Simple Text Formatter
req_text: Must treat blank lines as paragraph separators. Must not merge text across blank lines.

srd_title: cmd/fmt: Simple Text Formatter
req_text: Must preserve the indentation of the first line of each paragraph. Subsequent lines in the same paragraph are filled to match the second line's indentation (or the first if only one line).

srd_title: cmd/fmt: Simple Text Formatter
req_text: When given one or more FILE arguments, must read and format each file in order. When no file is given or "-" is given, must read from stdin.

srd_title: cmd/fmt: Simple Text Formatter
req_text: -w WIDTH or --width=WIDTH must set the maximum line width (default 75).

srd_title: cmd/fmt: Simple Text Formatter
req_text: -g GOAL or --goal=GOAL must set the goal line width. Lines are filled to approximately GOAL characters. Default goal is 93% of width.

srd_title: cmd/fmt: Simple Text Formatter
req_text: Must break lines at word boundaries (spaces). Must not break in the middle of a word unless the word exceeds the maximum width.

srd_title: cmd/fmt: Simple Text Formatter
req_text: Must collapse multiple spaces between words to a single space, except after sentence-ending punctuation (. ! ?) where two spaces are preserved.

srd_title: cmd/fmt: Simple Text Formatter
req_text: -s or --split-only must split long lines but not join short lines. Lines shorter than the goal width are left as-is.

srd_title: cmd/fmt: Simple Text Formatter
req_text: -u or --uniform-spacing must use one space between words and two spaces after sentence-ending punctuation uniformly.

srd_title: cmd/fmt: Simple Text Formatter
req_text: -p PREFIX or --prefix=PREFIX must only reformat lines beginning with PREFIX (after optional whitespace). Must remove the prefix before formatting and re-add it afterward.

srd_title: cmd/fmt: Simple Text Formatter
req_text: -t or --tagged-paragraph must treat the first line of each paragraph as having a different indentation from subsequent lines, preserving the tagged-paragraph format.

srd_title: cmd/fmt: Simple Text Formatter
req_text: Must exit 0 when formatting completes successfully.

srd_title: cmd/fmt: Simple Text Formatter
req_text: Must exit 1 when an invalid option is given or a file cannot be opened.

srd_title: cmd/fmt: Simple Text Formatter
req_text: Differential tests must compare stdout and exit codes between the Go binary and the reference binary via pkg/testutils.

srd_title: cmd/fmt: Simple Text Formatter
req_text: Tests must cover: default 75-char formatting, -w custom width, -g goal width, -s split-only, -u uniform spacing, -p prefix mode, -t tagged paragraph, multi-file input, stdin input, blank line paragraph boundaries, indentation preservation, and error cases (invalid width, missing file).

srd_title: cmd/numfmt: Convert Numbers from/to Human-Readable Strings
req_text: When given --to=UNIT, must convert each input number to a human-readable string with the appropriate suffix. UNIT is one of: si (powers of 1000), iec (powers of 1024), iec-i (powers of 1024 with 'i' suffix), or none.

srd_title: cmd/numfmt: Convert Numbers from/to Human-Readable Strings
req_text: When given --from=UNIT, must interpret each input number as a human-readable string with suffixes and convert to a raw number. UNIT values are the same as --to.

srd_title: cmd/numfmt: Convert Numbers from/to Human-Readable Strings
req_text: When neither --from nor --to is given, must pass numbers through unchanged.

srd_title: cmd/numfmt: Convert Numbers from/to Human-Readable Strings
req_text: Must read numbers from stdin (one per line) when no operands are given, or process command-line operands directly.

srd_title: cmd/numfmt: Convert Numbers from/to Human-Readable Strings
req_text: --format=FORMAT must use a printf-style format string for output (e.g., '%10f', '%.2f'). Must support width, precision, and left-alignment.

srd_title: cmd/numfmt: Convert Numbers from/to Human-Readable Strings
req_text: --padding=N must pad the output to N characters. Positive N right-aligns; negative N left-aligns.

srd_title: cmd/numfmt: Convert Numbers from/to Human-Readable Strings
req_text: --round=METHOD must control rounding: up (ceiling), down (floor), from-zero (away from zero), towards-zero (truncation), or nearest (default).

srd_title: cmd/numfmt: Convert Numbers from/to Human-Readable Strings
req_text: --suffix=SUFFIX must append SUFFIX to the output after the numeric value and any unit suffix.

srd_title: cmd/numfmt: Convert Numbers from/to Human-Readable Strings
req_text: --field=FIELDS must convert only the specified fields (1-indexed, comma-separated ranges like cut). Other fields are passed through unchanged.

srd_title: cmd/numfmt: Convert Numbers from/to Human-Readable Strings
req_text: -d DELIM or --delimiter=DELIM must use DELIM as the field delimiter for --field processing.

srd_title: cmd/numfmt: Convert Numbers from/to Human-Readable Strings
req_text: --header[=N] must pass through the first N lines (default 1) without conversion, treating them as headers.

srd_title: cmd/numfmt: Convert Numbers from/to Human-Readable Strings
req_text: --to-unit=N must scale the output by dividing by N before applying --to conversion. --from-unit=N must scale the input by multiplying by N before applying --from conversion.

srd_title: cmd/numfmt: Convert Numbers from/to Human-Readable Strings
req_text: Must exit 0 when all conversions complete successfully.

srd_title: cmd/numfmt: Convert Numbers from/to Human-Readable Strings
req_text: Must exit 2 when an invalid number is encountered (unless --invalid=ignore or --invalid=warn is set).

srd_title: cmd/numfmt: Convert Numbers from/to Human-Readable Strings
req_text: Differential tests must compare stdout and exit codes between the Go binary and the reference binary via pkg/testutils.

srd_title: cmd/numfmt: Convert Numbers from/to Human-Readable Strings
req_text: Tests must cover: --to si/iec/iec-i, --from si/iec, --format with width and precision, --padding, --round modes, --suffix, --field selection, --delimiter, --header, --to-unit/--from-unit, stdin and operand input, and error cases (invalid number, unknown suffix).

srd_title: cmd/od: Octal and Other Format Dump
req_text: When invoked with no type options, must display input in the default format: octal 2-byte words (equivalent to -t o2), with an octal address offset in the left column.

srd_title: cmd/od: Octal and Other Format Dump
req_text: -t TYPE or --format=TYPE must display input in the given format. TYPE consists of a format letter (a for named characters, c for C-style characters, d for signed decimal, f for floating point, o for octal, u for unsigned decimal, x for hexadecimal) optionally followed by a size in bytes.

srd_title: cmd/od: Octal and Other Format Dump
req_text: Multiple -t options may be given; each produces an additional line of output per input block.

srd_title: cmd/od: Octal and Other Format Dump
req_text: Must read from FILE arguments in order, or from stdin when no file is given or "-" is specified.

srd_title: cmd/od: Octal and Other Format Dump
req_text: -A RADIX or --address-radix=RADIX must set the address offset format. RADIX is d (decimal), o (octal), x (hexadecimal), or n (no addresses).

srd_title: cmd/od: Octal and Other Format Dump
req_text: -j BYTES or --skip-bytes=BYTES must skip BYTES input bytes before formatting. BYTES may have a multiplier suffix (b for 512, k for 1024, m for 1048576).

srd_title: cmd/od: Octal and Other Format Dump
req_text: -N BYTES or --read-bytes=BYTES must format at most BYTES input bytes.

srd_title: cmd/od: Octal and Other Format Dump
req_text: Must display a final line containing only the address of the byte past the last byte read (the file size offset).

srd_title: cmd/od: Octal and Other Format Dump
req_text: -w[N] or --width[=N] must set the number of input bytes per output line (default 16). When -w is given without a value, must use 32.

srd_title: cmd/od: Octal and Other Format Dump
req_text: Must support traditional short options as aliases for type specifiers. -b is equivalent to -t o1, -c is -t c, -d is -t u2, -o is -t o2, -s is -t d2, -x is -t x2.

srd_title: cmd/od: Octal and Other Format Dump
req_text: Duplicate bytes in multi-line output must be replaced with '*' on a line by itself to indicate repetition, matching GNU od behavior.

srd_title: cmd/od: Octal and Other Format Dump
req_text: -v or --output-duplicates must print all input data, disabling the '*' duplicate suppression.

srd_title: cmd/od: Octal and Other Format Dump
req_text: Must exit 0 when the dump completes successfully.

srd_title: cmd/od: Octal and Other Format Dump
req_text: Must exit 1 when an invalid option is given or a file cannot be opened.

srd_title: cmd/od: Octal and Other Format Dump
req_text: Differential tests must compare stdout and exit codes between the Go binary and the reference binary via pkg/testutils.

srd_title: cmd/od: Octal and Other Format Dump
req_text: Tests must cover: default octal dump, -t with each format letter (a, c, d, f, o, u, x) and size variants, -A address radix modes, -j skip bytes, -N read bytes, -w output width, -v output duplicates, traditional short options (-b, -c, -d, -o, -s, -x), multiple -t options, duplicate suppression with '*', stdin input, multi-file input, and error cases (invalid type, missing file).

srd_title: cmd/printf: Format and Print Data
req_text: Must interpret FORMAT as a printf-style format string containing literal text and conversion specifiers. Must print the formatted result to stdout with no trailing newline unless the format includes \n.

srd_title: cmd/printf: Format and Print Data
req_text: Must support integer conversion specifiers: %d (signed decimal), %i (signed decimal), %o (octal), %u (unsigned decimal), %x (lowercase hex), %X (uppercase hex).

srd_title: cmd/printf: Format and Print Data
req_text: Must support floating-point conversion specifiers: %f (decimal notation), %e (scientific notation), %g (shorter of %f and %e), and their uppercase variants %F, %E, %G.

srd_title: cmd/printf: Format and Print Data
req_text: Must support string conversion specifier %s and character conversion specifier %c. %b must interpret backslash escapes in the argument string (like echo -e).

srd_title: cmd/printf: Format and Print Data
req_text: Must support field width and precision in conversion specifiers (e.g., %10d, %.5f, %10.3f). Width specifies minimum field width; precision specifies digits after decimal for floats or maximum characters for strings.

srd_title: cmd/printf: Format and Print Data
req_text: Must support flag characters: '-' (left-align), '+' (always show sign), ' ' (space before positive numbers), '0' (zero-pad), '#' (alternate form).

srd_title: cmd/printf: Format and Print Data
req_text: Must support '*' for width and precision, taking the value from the next argument.

srd_title: cmd/printf: Format and Print Data
req_text: Must support '%%' as a literal percent character in the format string.

srd_title: cmd/printf: Format and Print Data
req_text: Must interpret C-style escape sequences in FORMAT: \\, \a, \b, \f, \n, \r, \t, \v, \NNN (octal), \xHH (hex), \uHHHH (Unicode), \UHHHHHHHH (Unicode).

srd_title: cmd/printf: Format and Print Data
req_text: When more arguments remain than the format consumes, must reuse the format string for the remaining arguments, repeating until all arguments are consumed.

srd_title: cmd/printf: Format and Print Data
req_text: When fewer arguments are provided than the format requires, must use 0 for numeric specifiers and empty string for string specifiers.

srd_title: cmd/printf: Format and Print Data
req_text: When a numeric argument starts with a single or double quote (e.g., '"A' or "'A"), must use the numeric value of the character that follows the quote.

srd_title: cmd/printf: Format and Print Data
req_text: Must exit 0 when formatting and printing complete successfully.

srd_title: cmd/printf: Format and Print Data
req_text: Must exit 1 when an invalid format directive is encountered or a numeric conversion fails. Must still produce partial output before the error.

srd_title: cmd/printf: Format and Print Data
req_text: Differential tests must compare stdout and exit codes between the Go binary and the reference binary via pkg/testutils.

srd_title: cmd/printf: Format and Print Data
req_text: Tests must cover: %d/%i/%o/%u/%x/%X integer formats, %f/%e/%g float formats, %s string, %c character, %b backslash-interpreted string, width and precision, all flag characters, '*' width/precision, argument recycling, escape sequences (\n, \t, \NNN, \xHH), character value arguments (quote prefix), missing arguments, and error cases (invalid format, non-numeric argument for %d).

srd_title: cmd/sha224sum: Compute and Check SHA-224 Message Digests
req_text: Must compute the SHA-224 digest of each named file and write one line per file in the format "HASH  FILENAME" (text mode) or "HASH *FILENAME" (binary mode). The default is text mode.

srd_title: cmd/sha224sum: Compute and Check SHA-224 Message Digests
req_text: Must read from stdin and print "HASH  -" when no file arguments are given or when "-" is provided as a filename.

srd_title: cmd/sha224sum: Compute and Check SHA-224 Message Digests
req_text: --tag must use BSD-style output format "SHA224 (FILENAME) = HASH".

srd_title: cmd/sha224sum: Compute and Check SHA-224 Message Digests
req_text: Must exit 1 when any named file cannot be opened, printing an error to stderr, and continue processing remaining files.

srd_title: cmd/sha224sum: Compute and Check SHA-224 Message Digests
req_text: --check FILE must read FILE, parse each line (GNU or BSD tag format), recompute the SHA-224 digest, and compare to the stored hash.

srd_title: cmd/sha224sum: Compute and Check SHA-224 Message Digests
req_text: Must print "FILENAME: OK" or "FILENAME: FAILED" for each entry. Must exit 1 if any check fails.

srd_title: cmd/sha224sum: Compute and Check SHA-224 Message Digests
req_text: --warn prints a warning for each malformed line. --quiet suppresses OK lines. --status suppresses all output.

srd_title: cmd/sha224sum: Compute and Check SHA-224 Message Digests
req_text: -b marks input as binary; output uses "HASH *FILENAME". -t (default) uses "HASH  FILENAME".

srd_title: cmd/sha224sum: Compute and Check SHA-224 Message Digests
req_text: --tag produces BSD tag format regardless of -b/-t.

srd_title: cmd/sha224sum: Compute and Check SHA-224 Message Digests
req_text: Must exit 0 when all files are processed and all verified digests match.

srd_title: cmd/sha224sum: Compute and Check SHA-224 Message Digests
req_text: Must exit 1 when any file cannot be opened, any digest fails, or the checksum file is unreadable.

srd_title: cmd/sha224sum: Compute and Check SHA-224 Message Digests
req_text: Must handle SIGPIPE gracefully (exit 0) using pkg/sys.InstallSIGPIPEHandler.

srd_title: cmd/base32: Base32 Encode and Decode

srd_title: cmd/base32: Base32 Encode and Decode

srd_title: cmd/df: Report Filesystem Disk Space Usage
req_text:
When invoked with no arguments, must list all mounted filesystems excluding
pseudo-filesystems (those with 0 total blocks), displaying one line per filesystem.
Default columns are: Filesystem, 1K-blocks, Used, Available, Use%, Mounted on.
Sizes are reported in 1024-byte block units.

srd_title: cmd/df: Report Filesystem Disk Space Usage
req_text:
Must print a header line as the first line of output. Column headers must match
GNU df exactly: "Filesystem", "1K-blocks", "Used", "Available", "Use%",
"Mounted on". Numeric columns (1K-blocks, Used, Available, Use%) are right-aligned.
Filesystem and Mounted on are left-aligned.

srd_title: cmd/df: Report Filesystem Disk Space Usage
req_text:
Use% is calculated as ceiling((total - available) * 100 / total) when total > 0.
When total is 0, Use% is displayed as a dash "-". The percentage is followed by
"%" with no space. Values are right-aligned in a column wide enough for "100%".

srd_title: cmd/df: Report Filesystem Disk Space Usage
req_text:
When one or more FILE arguments are given, must report the filesystem containing
each FILE rather than all filesystems. If a FILE does not exist, must print a
diagnostic to stderr and continue processing remaining arguments.

srd_title: cmd/df: Report Filesystem Disk Space Usage
req_text:
Column widths must be computed as per-column maxima of entry lengths across all
rows including the header, matching GNU df alignment. Fields are separated by
at least one space.

srd_title: cmd/df: Report Filesystem Disk Space Usage
req_text:
-h or --human-readable must display sizes using binary units (1024-based: K, M, G,
T, P, E) via pkg/format.HumanSize(bytes int64, opts HumanSizeOpts) string with
opts.Binary = true. The column header changes from "1K-blocks" to "Size". -h
applies to the Size, Used, and Available columns.

srd_title: cmd/df: Report Filesystem Disk Space Usage
req_text:
-H or --si must display sizes using SI units (1000-based: kB, MB, GB, TB, PB, EB)
via pkg/format.HumanSize(bytes int64, opts HumanSizeOpts) string with opts.Binary =
false. The column header changes from "1K-blocks" to "Size". -H applies to the
Size, Used, and Available columns.

srd_title: cmd/df: Report Filesystem Disk Space Usage
req_text: -h and -H are mutually exclusive. The last one on the command line takes precedence.

srd_title: cmd/df: Report Filesystem Disk Space Usage
req_text:
-T or --print-type must insert a "Type" column after the Filesystem column,
showing the filesystem type (e.g., apfs, ext4, tmpfs) for each entry.

srd_title: cmd/df: Report Filesystem Disk Space Usage
req_text:

become: Filesystem, Inodes, IUsed, IFree, IUse%, Mounted on. IUse% is calculated
the same way as Use% but using inode counts instead of block counts.

srd_title: cmd/df: Report Filesystem Disk Space Usage
req_text:

srd_title: cmd/df: Report Filesystem Disk Space Usage
req_text:

srd_title: cmd/df: Report Filesystem Disk Space Usage
req_text:

Multiple -t flags may be given to include multiple types. When -t is given,
only filesystems matching at least one specified type are shown.

srd_title: cmd/df: Report Filesystem Disk Space Usage
req_text:
-x TYPE or --exclude-type=TYPE must exclude filesystems of the specified type.
Multiple -x flags may be given. When both -t and -x are given, -t inclusion
is applied first, then -x exclusion.

srd_title: cmd/df: Report Filesystem Disk Space Usage
req_text:
--output or --output=FIELD_LIST must select which columns to display. When
--output is given without a field list, all available fields are shown. When
a comma-separated field list is given, only those fields appear in the specified

srd_title: cmd/dircolors: Color Setup for ls

to set and export LS_COLORS. The output format is:

export LS_COLORS
where <value> is the colon-separated list of type=code pairs derived from the
database.

srd_title: cmd/dircolors: Color Setup for ls
req_text:
When invoked with -c, --csh, or --c-shell, must output C shell commands to set
LS_COLORS. The output format is:
setenv LS_COLORS '<value>'
where <value> is the colon-separated list of type=code pairs.

srd_title: cmd/dircolors: Color Setup for ls
req_text:
When neither -b nor -c is given, must auto-detect the shell from the SHELL
environment variable. If SHELL ends with "csh" (e.g., /bin/tcsh, /bin/csh), use
C shell format. Otherwise use Bourne shell format. This matches GNU dircolors
auto-detection behavior.

srd_title: cmd/dircolors: Color Setup for ls
req_text:
-b and -c are mutually exclusive. The last one on the command line takes
precedence.

srd_title: cmd/dircolors: Color Setup for ls
req_text:
Must parse the GNU dircolors database format. Lines beginning with # are comments.
Blank lines are ignored. Each non-comment line has the form "KEYWORD value" where
KEYWORD is a file type name (e.g., DIR, LINK, EXEC, FIFO, SOCK, BLK, CHR, ORPHAN,
SETUID, SETGID, STICKY, OTHER_WRITABLE, STICKY_OTHER_WRITABLE, CAPABILITY,
MULTIHARDLINK) or a TERM entry, or a file extension (e.g., .tar, .gz, .jpg).

srd_title: cmd/dircolors: Color Setup for ls
req_text:

current TERM environment variable does not match any TERM line in the database,
must output an empty LS_COLORS value. When no TERM lines are present in the
database, the database applies to all terminals.

srd_title: cmd/dircolors: Color Setup for ls
req_text:
File type keywords map to two-letter LS_COLORS codes: DIR=di, LINK=ln, EXEC=ex,
FIFO=pi, SOCK=so, BLK=bd, CHR=cd, ORPHAN=or, SETUID=su, SETGID=sg, STICKY=st,
OTHER_WRITABLE=ow, STICKY_OTHER_WRITABLE=tw, CAPABILITY=ca, MULTIHARDLINK=mh,
NORMAL=no, FILE=fi, RESET=rs, MISSING=mi, LEFT=lc, RIGHT=rc, END=ec.
Extension entries (lines starting with . or *.) map to the full extension
pattern in LS_COLORS (e.g., "*.tar=01;31").

srd_title: cmd/dircolors: Color Setup for ls

database. When no filename is given (and -p is not given), must use the built-in

srd_title: cmd/dircolors: Color Setup for ls

srd_title: cmd/dircolors: Color Setup for ls

srd_title: cmd/dircolors: Color Setup for ls
